title: They stand behind their products!
body:
The Allen Edmonds Park Avenue is a classic. However, be aware that quality control can be somewhat of a problem and they do not stand behind their product. If you are lucky they last quite a while, and in this case one of my park ave fall apart within 4-5 months. They told me that the shoes need to be re-crafted and the warranty won't apply. I had a good experience with the manager, Curtis from the Bryant Park store, so I agreed to get it re-crafted for $125 with him. But buyer beware if you get a lemon you are out $125.

Edit: Even before they saw my review, one of the customer service associate, Allison was able to rectify the situation and agreed that this is actually a lemon and honored the warranty by sending me a new pair. I am very happy to learn that they do stand behind their products! Now I am confident that I can continue to recommend Allen Edmonds to everyone!

title: Stay away --- Quality control issues.
body:
I honestly was hoping that the pair of park avenue's that I ordered would not have any of these defects that other reviewers have mentioned, unfortunately I was severely mistaken.

1) The heel on the right shoe was not glued properly, and was coming apart. Seriously... Out of the box? Instant return.
2) There were bulges (small but noticeable) around the mouth of the shoe.
3) The ankle area already had creases in them.

I would stay away from ordering this shoe from amazon. I own a pair of nuemoks and absolutely love them. This pair was less than acceptable.

Btw, park avenues don't have metal eyelets as one of the negative reviewers states - not sure what he got, but they were not EA's.

title: Timeless shoe
body:
A college professor once told me that the first thing someone notices about you when you meet them is your shoes. As important as first impressions are, it's vital to be wearing a sharp pair of shoes that say you care about yourself.

These are a classic shoe that is not too flashy, but conservative and timeless.

Also, they're very comfortable.

title: Very expensive & VERY worth it
body:
I've always worn better than average shoes. When you wear size 13, you need good shoes. Anyway, one day I went berserk and bought a pair of
Allen Edmonds Men's Park Avenue Cap Toe Oxfords. They were comfortable from minute #1 and I haven't regretted the purchase for even a second. When I switched to my old good shoes for a week -- WOW what a difference. The Allen Edmonds shoes were much better. I now own two pairs and they are both great. I alternate them each day and use shoe trees at night -- both practices are highly recommended. One other note: Allen Edmonds shoe polish is excellent. I was using the brand you get at the grocery store and what a noticeable difference it makes to use the Allen Edmonds Premium Shoe Polish. Not sure why, but it is much better stuff. Bottom line: If you need excellent black dress shoes that are comfortable enough to wear for long days including long treks through airports, I highly recommend these. As for the price ... How much do you spend for tires on your car? My last set cost $500. I decided that I am worth $300 for awesome shoes.

title: Allen Edmonds has been bought and sold one time too many
body: I have worn Allen Edmonds' shoes 20+ years, it was a great run -- until my most recent pair. The new owners have cheapened every aspect of the shoe. Time for a new line of shoes.

title: This is not the cheapest by any means (certainly not the most expensive) but for someone who wants more quality than $100 shoes
body: I needed a conventional cap-toe balmoral shoes in affordable price. This is not the cheapest by any means (certainly not the most expensive) but for someone who wants more quality than $100 shoes that are being sold at department stores this is certainly a great step-up. The leather quality is wonderful and very comfortable once these are worn in. Fits so perfectly around my feet and there is no pain. (my pinkie can go in at the heel and  my toes are not smashed) I wear 7.5 D and this is the perfect size for me in 5-last shoes from AE. I also own Strand in Walnut and Fifth Avenue in Brown color. But this is the most formal pair and it gives me confidence knowing that if I need to dress up or be formal I can always rely on this pair. When I want to be little more fashionable (if the circumstances allow) I love wearing Strand Walnut. I like strand better to be honest but this is a go-to pair in a situation where I want to be safe and conservative. Goes great with my navy suit as well as grey but I like them with my charcoal/grey suit the most.

title: Sharp Shoes, but Mine "Bowed" at the Mouth
body:
These shoes are really sharp and comfortable, and I love Allen Edmonds in general. But strangely and unfortunately, when I wore these shoes, they "bowed" substantially around the mouth of the shoe, such that there was a 3/4" gap between my foot and the shoe. (I'll see if I can post a photo somewhere.)

I called Allen Edmonds' customer service and was told that the shoes aren't supposed to fit like that, and that it might be a glitch with the specific pair of shoes that I'd received. But, I went into Nordstrom the next day to try on a different pair of Park Avenues, and that pair bowed at the mouth too -- although not quite as much.

Bottom line, I think these are great shoes, and I'm really bummed that they didn't fit me correctly. I'm a little surprised that the shoes bowed like that, as my feet are a very standard size (10.5 D), and I've never had a problem like that with any other shoe. In light of my experience, I'd recommend that you try on these shoes at a store before you order them, just to ensure that you don't encounter the same problem that I did.

title: Great American Dress Shoe
body:
The Allen Edmonds Park Avenue is a classic dress shoe. It's perfect any time you have to wear a suit especially like weddings, funerals, job interviews, etc. The construction is solid with a clean, smooth calf skin upper. Don't expect the leather to soften or stretch very much (so make sure they fit correctly when you try them on). The Park Avenues fit true to size on me, but the shape of your foot may not be the same. Start with the Allen Edmonds fit guide which you can download from their website. Used correctly, the fit guide will give you a good starting point. There is no substitute for trying on a few different sizes of the shoe you want to buy, especially if it is your first pair of Allen Edmonds.

$300+ for dress shoes may seem expensive, but Allen Edmonds is a great value for the quality and style of shoe they offer. The full 360 Goodyear welt makes the shoe recraftable. For about $100 Allen Edmonds will resole and refinish the upper extending the life of your shoes. With the proper care, you can maintain them for ten years or more. Alden, the other American dress shoe, is typically more expensive at $400+ for the same style shoes. Recrafting at Alden runs about $160. So Allen Edmonds offers great quality at a more affordable price point. Shoes by John Lobb start at about $1200. Other makers like Crockett & Jones and JM Weston can only be found in New York City. Even Alden has a limited number of retailers. With Allen Edmonds, you can walk into any Nordstrom and try on a pair.

Allen Edmonds also stands behind their product. If the new shoes you receive aren't up to standard, send them back for a new pair. If you've been wearing a pair for a few weeks and find a defect, Allen Edmonds will fix it or replace it. I've never bought any product from shoes to TV sets that didn't occasionally come out as a lemon. The real question is what does the retailer or manufacturer do about it.

It took me several tries to find the right fit between Nordstrom, Amazon, and the Allen Edmonds store. I never had a hassle trying on or returning shoes that didn't fit or that didn't meet my standards for quality. But I did have to be patient. In the end, I have a great pair of dress shoes that help make me look good when I go to work.

title: The Gold Standard

I cannot recommend a better shoe. So far I'm liking this whole dressing like an adult thing. With the recrafting they offer, I'm looking forward to wearing these shoes for the next 20 years.

body: I'll just echo the other 5 star reviews here. Everything they've said is true. These shoes are incredibly comfortable, and they look great! First day I wore them to the office I got a ton of compliments. I look forward to buying another pair of allen edmonds very soon.

title: Best quality price rapport
body: As somewhat of a shoe maven (entirely too many pairs of shoes) I find Allen Edmonds not necessarily the best American made shoes (Alden are marginally better quality leather) but certainly the best quality/prix rapport. As a Brit I would stress that taking care of them is vital. In Britain the tradition is to buy fewer shoes but buy the best quality you can afford, don't wear them for more than one day at at time, always use shoe trees, and polish them with leather cream (never use a standard polish like Kiwi, it dries out the leather, I find Meltonian is the best). Your shoes will conform to your feet over time and you can then repair them (always ship them to Allen Edmonds, never take them to a local shoe repair shop). You can then expect to keep the shoes for decades and the overall cost will actually be lower than buying cheaper shoes and throwing them away.

title: How do I score a shoe that didn't fit at all???
body: Part of me feels badly for giving this a 2-star review (don't like it), but what should I do? I normally wear an 11.5D (medium) dress shoe (Johnston & Murphy and Bostonian). So I ordered that in the Park Avenue. It was longer than any 11.5D I have ever worn, closer to what I normally see as a 12. So I ordered 11 D and E (medium and wide). The 11D was too narrow in the middle of my foot and pressed in a bit on my big toe. The 11E was good in the toes and middle of my foot but there was a large gap all around where my ankle comes into the shoe. I could stick a finger in any spot and the shoe wouldn't touch it. This made the back of the shoe very loose and unsecured feeling. The leather was very nice and soft for a new dress shoe and seemed to be of good quality, but the last this shoe was built on doesn't work for me at all. So, what am I supposed to write, eh? Bummer.

One time, I returned a pair to a store clerk at the Palo Alto store.. the female worker replied "oh just the inside?" with "go F yourself" attitude. title: Do your research, then buy this shoe!
body:
The AE Park Ave is the perfect entry shoe for those looking to step up (get it?) their wardrobe. The burnished brown is probably the most versatile color that can be worn with any suit that's not black and also dressed down with denim. Make sure to purchase these from an authorized retailer like Amazon - don't go poking around Nord rack for these where you're likely to run into sub-par/second-quality shoes. AE's have a pretty sizeable following, so you'll also be able to find answers to almost any question with a quick search. A few notes:

Sizing: As with almost any dress shoes these will run about 1/2 a size large (ie if you wear 10.5 in Nike running shoes, you're probably a 10 in these). I can't stress enough the importance of doing the proper research and figuring out your exact size, including width. If you have to, go to the local shoe store and get measured (surprisingly...most guys don't actually know their true shoe size). Don't be tempted to compensate for width by sizing up. For example, if size 10E is out of stock, don't be tempted to order a 10.5D. You might be able to get away with this other makers, but it'll make a big difference to nail the sizing with these. They will be the most comfortable dress shoes you own. As the description says, the cork footbed will conform to your foot in a few weeks, and it'll feel like this shoe was made for your feet.

Durability: I'm a huge fan of brown dress shoes because they tend to develop beautiful patinas over time and simply age better than black shoes do. The Park Aves are no different here - you can find endless pictures on the internet of how well AE's age. The soles are welted so that when you do wear through them in a few years (and you will be wearing these a lot, trust me) you can get them recrafted by AE for $100 or so (you can also take it to the local cobbler). Basically these shoes will lost you a long, long time.

Care: these actually hold up really well without much babying, but if you're going to drop $300+ on shoes, you might as well take care of them. At the very least use cedar shoe trees (the kind with adjustable width) and brush/polish once a month or so. The AE website has sales on shoe care products pretty often that ship free.

Value: Not everyone can afford custom made John Lobbs or C&J's (personally I don't see the reason for spending that much on shoes anyway). My only gripe is that prices have creeped up year after year, but that's expected with sourcing and labor costs increasing. If you're waffling between AE's and say, a pair of $175 Johnston & Murphys or even $100-150 shoes from Macy's, do yourself a favor and go with the AE's. Sure, you could buy 2 or 3 pairs for the price of one pair of Park Aves, but the AE's will not only last much longer, but they will look better over time and be more comfortable.

Overall, an excellent way to quite literally transform your wardrobe. After all, if Park Aves are good enough for the President of the United States, they're surely good enough for you!

title: Beautiful shoes.... Lasted a year...
body: After much research, I bit the bullet and invested in a nice paid of these Allen Edmund Men's Park Avenue Cap-Toe Oxford. They are very comfortable, and certainly make a statement. I purchased them about a year ago. About 3 months ago, the seams on the right show started to wither. They eventually severed and shortly after, the bottom leather sole began to separate from the bottom of the shoe. I continued to wear them everyday, knowing soon enough, my feet would eventually become wet. Well, today was the day. As I got out of my car, the front half of the sole, almost all the way to the heel, separated and began flapping about. I finally cut the sole off just so I could walk without looking like a hobo. The left shoe would be as bad if I wore them another few weeks, but both shoes have since been remanded to the trash can. Very disappointing. Spent really good money on, for the most part, really good shoes, but they just didn't last. *In full disclosure, I have had this issue with other shoes I have worn over the years so it may be ME more than the shoes. I have a distinct stride in which my right foot makes uneven contact with the ground, rubbing the interior side of my right shoe disproportionately. This creates uneven wear on the inside of my right show, and has taken many "souls" over the years, if you will pardon the pun.

title: Great shoe super customer service
body:
I am so satisfied with the quality and appearance of Allen Edmonds shoes I no longer shop for any other brand. Last year I bought the Park Avenue and was greatly pleased the shoe. Unfortunately, it developed a crease that was uncomfortable in the toe cap part of the shoe. When I contacted the company they had me send back the shoe for repair. The outcome was a new pair of shoes arriving at my door two weeks later!

It is great to know that such a fine American product is backed by the kind of customer service one hopes for when purchasing a shoe that is expected to last for a lifetime.

title: No better value for the price.
body:
I purchased this pair as my first Allen Edmonds at the behest of two people, my grandfather (who has several pairs that are 15+ years old, and still look like new), and my best friend who recently acquired his first pair and had good things to say.

I was not disappointed.

Right out of the box, it's easy to note how much more distinguishedly handsome and well made these shoes are compared to competitors (or shoes selling for 1/3 the cost, which aren't even considered competition b/c they are selling to a different market).

I must say, they did feel stiff for the first few wears, but just last week I noted that they were remarkably more comfortable than at first.

Just a few helpful notes:

1) Get something for the sole bottoms. Leather soles aren't great at providing traction on carpet (at least not on the carpet at my office.

2) Go to the AE website and read about their lasts, as shoes created on different lasts have different overall fits.

3) On the AE website, you will also find a sizing chart which you can print out and use to determine your appropriate size in AE shoes. It will save you time in returns, and provide a shoe that fits you best!

Enjoy your new Allen-Edmonds!!!

title: Best dress shoes I've ever owned
body:
Got these shoes as a gift from my father-in-law a year ago (in brown). The first day I wore these shoes I walked over a mile continuously on asphalt and didn't have a minute of discomfort.

I've also noticed that these shoes hold their shape and look a lot better than others as they age. My father-in-law has a pair of Park Avenue's that look just as new as mine, and they're about 15 years old. My brother got a pair of Bostonian's the same year I got these and they look like they're about 10 years older than mine.

The tip from my father-in-law that has kept mine in good shape: Use the Premium Shoe Polish, not the wax shoe polish. Their premium polish is oil, not wax, based. This means that you're re-hydrating the leather and keeping it supple every time you polish it.

If you use a wax polish the leather will gradually dry out unless you strip the wax and recondition the leather. Dry leather not only cracks, but easily absorbs liquid, so it's much easier to get a bad stain from salty slush on the side of the road.

title: Quality, comfortable, great brand
body:
These are awesome entry level shoes into the higher end mens dress shoes segment. I would say that range is about $300-700 for quality (I'm talking able to last 7+ years with maintenance) shoes. The great thing about Allen Edmonds (besides being made in the USA) are that they are entirely re-craftable, meaning you can get the soles, heals, leather all completely replaced. If you were to wear these shoes out completely, AE will basically re-craft them with all new parts for about a third of the cost of a new pair. So you can start to see where the idea of "investing" in a good pair of shoes comes in. The price will be high today, but having one excellent pair that can last 7 years easily pays for itself vs. buying a brand new pair of lesser quality shoes every 1-2 years after they wear out.

Give yourself about a month to break these in. The cork souls are very hard, and take a while to form to your foot. Once they do though, it's like having orthotics in your shoes. The cork forms perfectly around your foot, and stays that way, never loosing shape like foam in a sneaker eventually does. I got a couple of minor blisters while wearing these over the first month, but now they fit like a glove.

**Another major tip: IF YOU'VE NEVER BOUGHT FROM AE BEFORE- go to a physical store and try on a pair for sizing. These do not fit like typical sneakers or other brands of dress shoes. They offer like 5 different widths as well, so its critical to get fitted by a professional so that you're truly getting your money's worth. Even the most expensive sneakers are completely useless if they don't fit you correctly.

title: Major Break In Pains - Quick Wear
body:
UPDATE: I took my shoes into an Allen Edmunds store and they were very helpful. They've taken the shoes back even though I didn't buy it from them and are replacing them with a new pair that should fit me better. Also, they are getting me a pair with their new V-Tread bottoms which are rubber shoes on top of the leather to protect them from excess wear when wearing them every day (on business travel). All-in-all very happy with the customer service. Let's hope the break-in on this new pair goes smoothly!

I'm four business days into breaking in my new pair of Park Avenue's and I've gotta say it's been the most painful break in period I've ever experienced. The crease on one of the shoes digs into the top of my foot and the pain makes it hard to walk (or to think for that matter). I just flipped the shoes over and the leather soles have already started to wear considerably (after only four days) to the point where it's noticeable when looking at the shoe from the front and is has also broken the stiches that hold the leather sole onto the shoe. I may have bought the wrong shape last for my foot, but needless to say I was expecting a lot more after hearing all of the raving about this brand.

title: Best dress shoes I've ever had
body:
I am cursed with bunions. Be glad you are not because finding comfortable shoes, dress or otherwise, is often a challenge. At the time of purchase, I could not have been more disappointed in myself for spending over $300 on a pair of shoes. Pricey clothing is not my thing, but after wearing these classics a few times, I was without remorse.

Allen Edmonds quality is top notch, and the comfort is second to no other dress shoe that I have walked in on city streets. It is now 7 months since I purchased these shoes, and I am an extremely satisfied customer. I will be buying another pair of Allen Edmonds very soon.

title: lovely shoes, but first fit in a shop...
body:
These are the best shoes that I own and my first premium pair. The quality is fantastic and far greater than any other shoe that I have previously owned. The leather is very fine and they are crafted very nicely. No quality issues that I can perceive.

I recommend that before you buy, try these on in person. They fit quite tightly and my regular size of 10D was too tight, resulting in my moving up to 10E. Even then the shoes are snug but do not pinch. Definitely different from what I am used to.

I got this pair for special occasions as I don't think I can waste them for daily office wear. Have worn them a couple of times to ensure that they are "broken in". Have come to the conclusion that this is not really necessary. They remain snug but not uncomfortable and there were no problems during the days.

The main issue that I have with them is that they came without shoe trees. At this price level I think that AE should have included shoe trees with them. The packaging is very nice and each shoe has its own bag. Seeing as most users will be first timers without prior experience AE has missed out on an opportunity to do some marketing by adding a small user guide, cleaning supplies etc.

Nonetheless, highly recommended for anyone looking for a great pair of shoes.

title: Rainbow Single Layer Sierra Color Sandals
body:

My shoe size is 11.5 wide and I wore XL fine on my previous two pair but had to bump up to XXL on this pair. Not a problem, just not sure what to make of it. Rainbows are notorious for their break in period, and these were no different. But the difference is that my older pairs took about a week to break in, these took about 3 weeks. After two blisters, redness, and pain they are now molded to my foot and the most comfortable sandals I've ever owned. Please allow for a lengthy break in period. They'll reward you in spades. Also, my other pairs were virtually indestructible, whereas this pair seem to stain much easier and already the outer heel is starting to show some wear. It might just be me, but it seems this new pair isn't up to the quality of the older pairs due to the before mentioned occurrences. (These are high quality, just seems a step below my older ones.) I dunno. Still the most comfortable sandals I've ever worn.
Just allow for break-in. Highly recommended.

title: Outstanding casual/work boot (even though made in Thailand)
body:
Many reviewers note that the good old version made in Australia was much higher quality than the new version made elsewhere. Well, mine say "Made in Thailand" and they are excellent, high-quality boots.

I bought them while visiting my fiancee in Chicago, because it was miserably slushy and I only had light leather shoes. Glad I did! Below the elastic they are waterproof and warm, without being too warm.

They fit well, and stay firm around the foot despite walking, running, bounding up stairs, etc (I'm pretty high-energy), even without laces. In fact, I absolutely HATE having to lace/unlace shoes, so they hit a home run for convenience.

The brown color is versatile - not too dark for light-colored pants (though too dark for white pants), but still dressy enough to pair with deep blue jeans or navy pants. The style is pretty casual, more like a work boot than a dress boot, and the leather is solid and durable.

They are comfortable to wear. Blundstone touts their shock-absorbing qualities, but I don't notice a difference from normal shoes. However, their 'moisture-wicking' soles really *DO* work, as my feet have never gotten sweaty in these boots.

I eased up wearing them recently because they got some nicks on the toe. The leather almost seems like plastic or rubber, it's so dense, and I didn't know what to do (and wasn't sure I could polish them). But eventually I pulled out my old shoe-shine kit and went to work with brown polish and the old cloth...bingo. They actually look a bit more dressy shined up, and while I had to work to get the polish in the nicks, the shoe looks almost new.

Overall this is an amazingly convenient, comfortable, and handsome casual boot. I will be buying more Blundstones - even those made out of Australia - and I'm greedily eyeing their 062 style dress boots.

title: Getting Blundstone 500 Size Right
body:
Update, 07-12-22: While I stand by my initial review of my Blundstone 500s, I want to add that at this time the molded foam midsoles are desintegrating. This happened to my Vasque hiking boots, too; but it took over 30 years! Anyway, I just fished my Blundstones out of the closet, and a large chunk has fallen out the front of one boot, and the sole is peeling off, and both midsoles feel friable, meaning decomposition will only go faster from here. Otherwise, the boots are in great shape, as would be expected, as they got little wear over the 3 years it took for the midsole to break down. Caveat emptor.

Original review:
It took me 3 tries to get the right size Blundstone 500s, and I recommend doing some research before purchasing these boots. The size basics are these: The Australian whole size Blundstone is an American E width and a full size longer than an American size boot. The half size up is literally no longer or wider but is is "roomier" inside than the whole size under it. I wear a 10 E American boot, and the Australian size 9 Blundstones fit me well enough that I kept them. My feet simply swim in the 9 1/2., despite it is - literally - exactly the same length and width as the 9. As for quality, these boots are not like Limmers or Whites but they are well made by today's standards for mass produced boots. The leather is not at all soft, rather it has a firm hand, like a good work boot, and it takes a while to break them in. The insole is nothing special, and the heal counter is stiff. The mid-sole gives some support, not a lot. The sole is medium soft. Overall, the 500 offers more support than my Clark's Desert Boots and less than typical work boots I've opted for over the years. I would not use them for construction work involving extension ladders or shovels, but they are fine for uneven terrain and doing chores. I wear them daily as a construction superintendent. For this they are more comfortable than my Red Wing 952s, yet another American made boot that's not what it once was.

title: Slow Shipping from Amazon
body: I just got a pair of Mens' Blundstone Boots ordered from Amazon. The price was competitive (same as Village Shoes, New York, etc) and they charged for shipping. Placed the order 11-14 and did not arrive until 11-23, 9 days later. They came from Amazon in Kentucky address and I am in San Francisco area. Worse part was that they shipped USPS (US Postal Service). We thought they would come by UPS and web site stated it would be no more than 5 days. They arrived more than 5 working days after we ordered them. We even got an email from Amazon that the USPS could not deliver then because of our address, could not find us, though we are one of biggest buildings in town and get mail and packages every day. I had to go to Post Office, and despite fact that I had an email from Amazon saying there were shipped by USPS, the USPS said that they knew nothing about it, didn't know where it was  and insisted it was UPS that was at fault though UPS didn't have anything to do with it. We had no tracking number from Amazon and had no idea where they were coming from. The did not send an email notice when the boots were shipped. We finally tracked down the box at Post Office and got the boots. Think twice before you order and check how the merchandise will be sent. I will never order anything again that comes via USPS, and will make sure it's either UPS or FedEx. The boots are wonderful, soft, comfortable, can't wait to wear them around

title: Best shoe ever
body: This is my first pair of blundstones. I purchased a half size larger so that I could wear slightly thicker socks. I cannot wear my thickest socks as I normally could sizing up, so they seem to be sized slightly smaller. I ordered an 8.5 US or 5.5 AU. I would probably order the same size again in the future, because it works well with thin socks as well and I can wear these boots in the winter or the summer. Super lightweight boot. I have really high arches/instep, so the first week my arch was uncomfortable but the boots broke in quickly. Though the arch support isn't the best, I actually have no pain or issues wearing them and just use the standard sole insert already provided. These boots are stiff at first, but tailor to your foot/soften after constant wear really fast. They are also so incredibly durable and do not scrape up easily - marks are easy to wipe off/clean. I have had these shoes for over 6 months and they still look new after wearing them almost every single day. I think they'll last a few years.

title: Do yourself a favor...
body:
Do yourself a favor and purchase a pair from a brick and mortar. I didn't buy my 10875s from Azon

Advantages:
You'll be professionally fitted (my first impression on their foot pressure machine was it's gimmicky, more later).
You'll support your local community.
You don't have to play shoe tag to get a pair that fits.

Disadvantage:
They may not have the color or style you want in stock, but will order for you.

I give them 4 stars but added a star because they're Red Wing boots. The sole may wear out faster than Vibram waffle lugs but this is ok with me because this type of sole is soft walking. I work on roof tops, gravel roads, metal grates, they won't track pea gravel all over and into your truck. Like I said, soft walking is more important.

I have widish feet, Neanderthal thick ankles sized right between a 10-11. I bought the 11D, perfect fit. Still they are a little roomy even with my feet while wide, don't meet a measured E. The 11Ds were a perfect fit (with teh Red Wing logo, not sure why these don't seem to have it).

I was surprised I could get my feet into them, the horse like ankle structure thing. I went back and forth between two sizes and widths, four pairs of boots, thankfully I didn't have to play shoe tag with an online retailer to get what I needed. Unfortunately, the boot fits perfectly size wise, but because of high arches and cow ankles I can't add a foot bed. The good news is the boot is fitting to my feet and high arches, I have little discomfort as time goes by.

About their magic foot plant pressure machine. It looked like a high tech man behind the curtain charade. I wanted to buy some 1907s (the last doesn't work for me) but the store owner had me try it out again (second store, this one local). She rec'd an insole and took them back and tried them in the 10875, sucked, expensive, couldn't get my feet into them.

Bingo, I have a pair of Danner Bull Run Cristy boots that I despised. I tried the insoles in them and the boot was transformed.

Five stars, I guess not really, unless you get what you paid for. I feel I did.

title: Red Wing size
body:
1st time to own Red Wing shoes. Been reading about them and know I should go down 1/2 a size for them to fit right. I am naturally 10.5US, and so I got a size 10US. With this model, I think I could have gone a full size down but I will be wearing thick socks with these boots and 1/2 is just right.

Will update my review once I've had the pair for a longer time.

Edit (Update after 2-3 months):

I have never experienced such comfy boots!!!!

BUT.....

The first 3-5 wears were HELL!!!! It came to a point that I had to put duct tape on my heals to prevent blisters. But after breaking them in (around after the 5th wear), they have become very comfortable!!!!! Yes, they are heavy, but somehow you don't feel the weight! Great boots!!!!

Some tips:
1. They do run 1 to 1/2 size bigger. As mentioned, I use 10.5 in other shoes and got a 10D for Red Wing moc toes. They fit great! I also tried a friend's brand new pair (Abilene Moc Toe) which was 9.5E and it also fit! (But I think getting an E width is harder than the usual D).
2. Wear thick socks;
3. Tie em up tight -- this will help reduce slippage which could give you blisters;
4. BUT not too tight as I also got some soreness at the part of my leg where the top of the boot was rubbing against;
5. Wear em as often to break em in faster!

I have become a Red Wing fan! Have already ordered my second RW, this time an Iron Ranger (friends swear there is no / minimal break in period).

Will try to update this review again.

title: Make sure you check the date on the label inside the tongue
body:
The intent of my review is to make buyers aware of what to look for if and when you order these Red Wing Heritage boots from Amazon. I'm normally a size 12 or 12.5 in normal shoes and also have a removable orthotic footbed that in place in all my shoes due to my high arches. I ordered 2 pairs of Red Wing Heritage Moc 6" boots in Briar Oil Slick from Amazon in size 11.5 and 11. I recently purchased a pair of the Red Wing Heritage chukkas boots in briar oil slick and the 11.5 fit me perfectly. I liked the chukkas so much I ordered the 6" boots. When I purchased the chukkas, the person at the Red Wing Store showed me on the tag on the inside of the tongue of the boot that my chukkas were made on "10/15" - essentially since I purchased the chukkas in December, they were made 2 months prior.

The 6" moc boots in size 11.5 arrived first from Amazon and when I opened the box, the first thing I noticed was how the boots looked "broken in" and the leather was faded, dried out, and old. The first thing I did was look at the label on the tongue and noticed the date was 2011 - these boots were almost 5 years old! Yet Amazon was selling them as "new." I tried the boots on, just to get a gauge on size and found the 11.5s to be too big. So I returned them. However, if they had fit, I would have certainly complained to Amazon for trying to sell me a new pair of expensive Red Wing boots that were obviously old and not up to any sort of Red Wing standards. Buyers - be aware of this issue and make sure you check the date the boot was made on the tag inside the tongue - the date is on the lower, right part of the boot below the model number. It's one thing if the boots are a few years old and still look brand new, but the boots Amazon sent me were definitely sub-par.

2 days later the size 11 6" moc boots arrived and I wasn't sure what to expect. I opened the box and immediately inspected the boots for quality and the date they were made. Fortunately, the date was "10/15" so I was sure these were recently made. While the boots looked as if someone had tried them on before, I could tell the size 11 was perfect for me and the boot fit great. The color of the briar oil slick along with the crepe sole looks amazing. I've been wearing them around the house for about a week now and I hate having to take them off. Every time I wear them they get more and more comfortable. I think of them as more comfortable than my favorite pair of running shoes, but the Red Wings provide far more support. I am very happy with the 6" moc boot and actually find them easier to break in than my chukkas. Once you decide on a color(s), and once you find your fit, I think just like my you will be sold on Red Wing Heritage boots. I am using these for wearing in the office, out in the field (construction), and for style around town.

I think you should think hard not only about the boots but about what type of insole you require.  The permanent leather insole in these is inadequate for my needs, on it's own.  I tried numerous insoles in these trying to find something that was cushioned enough without making the boot too tight.  I put baggies of water in the boots and froze them to stretch them at least 4 times, and could not get them to stretch enough to make them fit comfortable.  I was about ready to give up and try to sell the boots.  Out of desperation I bought a bottle of shoe stretch liquid.  I put in my new sof soles thin insoles.  sprayed the inside and outside of the boot.  then I put on 2 pairs of thick wool socks, soaked in shoe stretch.  I crammed my feet into the boots and wore then around the house for 4 hours.  Once they were completely dry they fit like a glove.  For casual wear they are as comfortable as any show I own.  In summary, if you wear thick insoles don't size down a full size, and if you do size down prepare for the time investment.  Once you invest they time they are great.  Nearly every time I wear them someone compliments me on them.

body:
It took me about eight weeks of almost daily wear to get these boots broken in to where they fit without chafing and heel slip... and pain and blood and blisters. The initial fit was extremely uncomfortable, but after reading numerous articles online I learned that this is normal for Red Wing boots, and that the break-in process is, indeed, a process; a process that requires time, patience, and a fair amount of discomfort.

Now, a bit over two months after receiving them, these are my daily wear boots. I wear them for work, for hiking, and as my general purpose shoes. After my initial dismay at the level of discomfort during the break-in process, I'm at the point where I'm seriously considering purchasing a second pair.

As for fit, I ordered the same size I wear in Converse All-Stars sneakers. Some people recommend sizing up, others recommend sizing down. Depends on what you're comparing them to, I guess.

title: Great shoes
body:
Clarks Desert Boots are my favorite all-purpose shoes. I actually own 3 pairs of them in different colors. My oldest pair I've been wearing for over four years! The sole is great quality and very durable. If they do break you can get them resoled for relatively cheap which extends the longevity of the shoes. The material is also quite comfortable and I think all of the colors look better with age.

I wear these shows on a regular basis to work, school, and when I go out. I typically wear bootcut/slim fit jeans and pants and these shoes pair well with either fit. They can also work well with shorts so you can wear them in warmer weather!

These shoes do run about a size large, so I typically buy them a size down. I wear 9.5 normally but get 8.5 for these shoes.

This particular color, the metallic black, is pretty sleek looking. I got this over the regular suede which looks a little plain (plus I don't like suede that much). My only complaint is that the material is shiner than expected and the material is kinda stuff (but this will probably soften with time).

title: Not worth the Time or Money!
body: These boots take FOREVER to break in. Don't plan on wearing white socks for a few months, because the leather soles inside the shoe will permanently stain any white socks you wear an awkward orange color. The boots once broken in are comfortable and tough. After 6 months one of the seams busted and my foot was completely exposed whenever I put weight on my toe. After 9 months the sole of this shoe is completely smooth, and I stopped wearing them because I would fall if the bottoms made contact with anything wet. For this price you expect more... I understand shoes like this need to be re-soled every year. But 9 months is not acceptable, and that is after tears in the seams and several months of breaking in. Look for something better, I have bought a pair of Wolverine 1000 miles that are comfortable out of the box, and have been through a beating and held up better than these Red Wings. I have an older pair of Wolverines that I have owned for years with minimal repairs and damage. I continue to wear the older pair over the Red Wings. If you want a stylish boot you can wear for special occasions... this might be for you, but if you want a boot that you can kick off after a hard days work for years to come... This is not your shoe. I am disappointed Red Wing, I gave this company and this boot a full year and was unimpressed by the result.

title: Best shoes I own
body:
I've wanted a pair of Red Wing boots for a long time. I finally went ahead and ordered a pair from Amazon. For some reason, the size I needed was $90 less than all the other sizes. I couldn't pass up that deal! I've tried them on a few times locally, so I knew the size I needed. And I ordered the same size I normally wear in other brands of shoes. They fit perfectly. I understand why some people give negative reviews. They do take a while to break in. And don't wear them with thin socks! I wear them with a pair of SmartWool midweight merino wool socks and they are super comfortable.

I initially thought I'd prefer the moc style, but the round toe is truly "classic". I did not buy these for outdoor 'work'. I wear them to work, but I could wear any shoe I wanted when I go to work, anything from flip-flops, to running shoes, to leather boots. These are just perfect for late fall/winter. I'll go back to my flip-flops in the spring. I even wore them to church last weekend.....

You know you want them, so just place the order.

title: O.K, but not the best!
body:
Red Wing Heritage Men's Classic Work 6-Inch Round Toe Boot - Suede: are made well.
I have owned mine fore a month now, and the suede still smells oily and they feels soft.
I have worn these several times and have walked about 2 miles in one stretch, but they are not completely broken in yet, despite this. I wonder about how long it will require. The soles are real stiff, so that long walk, although comfortable, left my feet knowing I'd done it.
I have added Red Wing insoles to soften them, and that helps much.
Beautiful color and workmanship. I chose the Slate Blue and believe it will add some fair to your already handsomeness.
If not for the stiff soles, and the rawhide laces, that require sometime to soften, I'd say these boots were tops. These laces took a few times before they stay. Maybe I need to tie them in the type of tie you'd use for a child?
When warmed up, they seem to do better. I'll have to give them a pass, being this is my first experience with laces made this way. They do look nice though.

title: At first these felt small and I needed about a month before they started to feel more or less comfortable. I wear them almost daily for the good ...
body:
Time flies. Two years have passed since I bought these. Replaced S-Lab 3 which served me well for 3-4 years.
At first these felt small and I needed about a month before they started to feel more or less comfortable.
I wear them almost daily for the good part of the year. Mostly for casual walking, but they have seen some light tracks and running sessions.
After 2 years half sole height is gone. More than half probably. The upper part shows wear as well. So Slab 6 seems half as durable as Slab 3 was.

Even though the quality of Salomon shoes seems to decrease over the years, it's not yet gone, so my next pair is probably be Salomon again.

The problem I am having is that they are so uncomfortable to walk in or run with. I have medium arches and thought they would be fine. I am a big fan of soloman products but feel that this was the wrong purchase for me. That being said I have owned several pairs of Salomon's before and never had a problem. I will not be purchasing them online again, as the obvious (to me) problem is that I didn't try them on for any length of time or I would have known I couldn't wear them. I would still recommend Salomon's to any buyer that has previously worn these or at least tried them on somewhere.

title: Answered my poor knees' prayers!
body:
So this year I've found a love for running. I started with a great pair of comfortable shoes that I chose mainly for that - comfort. I should have chosen a pair specifically for my overpronation, but I knew nothing about all that until the pain set in. Over the course of a month I added on too many miles and as a result, injured my knees to where I was devastated because I could hardly walk up and down stairs anymore. Enter the kayanos.
I went to a running store, found out all about the way I run, and was ultimately torn between this at the GT-2000 2. I chose these in the end, because of comfort purposes. They are brilliant. They are extremely padded, and yet I feel like I can still feel the ground. I put them on, went for a 2 miler expecting disappointment and instead came back with that runner's high I've missed so much since hurting myself.
They are as most everybody says they are. Reliable. Comfortable. Stable. Pricey, for sure, but worth the investment. My knees think so anyway.

Cheers!

title: Best hiking/camp/boating shoe you can get for the $$
body:
These were purchased as my backpacking water crossing and camp shoes. After a full day of wearing hiking boots, it's nice to take a break and let your feet breathe with these on. I switch to them as soon as I get to camp, or whenever I take an extended break on the trail. Awesome for river crossings because they have decent tread and they're not going to get sucked off your feet like regular flip flops. They are amazingly light so I have no issue with pack weight when I tie them to the outside of my pack to keep them dry and handy. The straps are nice and strong with plenty of velcro across the straps for even the widest feet/angle adjustments.

These are now also my kayaking sandals. They dry fast, fit comfortable, and give me plenty of traction and foot support when walking on submerged rocks and gravel.

Can't beat the original Teva sandals for a lightweight and reliable outdoor shoe.

title: Comfortable and great for foot problems
body:
This is the fourth pair of Orthoheels that I have purchased. I am happy to see that they are making them more stylish looking. I have plantar fasciitis which has been very painful in my heel so I have been careful of what I am wearing. The arch and heel cup in these flip flops are great and I can wear them all day. They help to alleviate the pain more than most of the shoes and shoe inserts that I have tried. They are also really good for people that have a tendency to pronate since they have good arch support. The footbed in some of the Orthoheels are a harder rubber and some of them have a softer footbed and both feel good. The Vionics seem to feel more comfortable than my older Orthoheels. Another favorite of mine for comfort is Mephisto.
If you are a first time buyer of Othoheel, take care in sizing. I am an 8 1/2 in shoes and sandals and I order an 8 in Orthoheel and they have all fit perfectly in that size.
The shoes are made in a nice and sturdy fashion. There doesn't seem to be a risk of breaking straps. As I mentioned earlier, they are much more fashionable looking than they were previously. I just wish that they would use more leather on some of the shoes instead of a pleather look but for the price I guess that it can be overlooked.

title: Break in  and double check your cart
body:
Ive been obsessed with blundstones for a long time and finnally gave. The quality and attractiveness of the shoe is amazing however the size is a whole different ball game.
Ive returned these shoes 3 times. Twice, I got sent the wrong size because the link to a 5.5 added a 4.5 into my cart so of course I got the shoe’s and squashed my feet into them only to realize I was sent the wrong size. Then, once discovering how to order the correct size, its too small as well. I would recomend going up a full size in these shoes especially if youre using them as winter boots and want heavy socks. The heal and rim of the shoe rub really bad and Im sure will be better once broken in but are incredibly uncomfortable as of now. Be aware that these shoes take a while to break in and are not great for wide high arches.

title: Be patient

Like a lot of high-quality shoes, the break-in time is worth the investment, but you gotta be prepared to hate them for while first.

body: I'll start by saying I bought these boots for their function, a sturdy slip on boot that I can work all day in, going indoors and out, from cutting firewood to shaping sourdough for hours. The leather softened up after a few days, they never felt too loose or tight, the elastic opening feels good, no hot spots on my feet and not too heavy at all. I've really enjoyed them. The only con is that the standard insole is pretty cheap. It doesn't offer much support or cushion, which is a bummer when you work 8-10 hours on your feet. I've ordered some work boot insoles that I think will do the trick. For the price, I just expected nicer insoles. Still, I'm quite happy with these ;)

title: Love Sperry's, not so much the sole.
body: These shoes are awesome. The shipping was fast and everything, but there was a problem. The soles are annoying as hell when they start to peel. I have another pair that I got from an actual sperry carrying store instead of online and the soles have never even started to look like they will peel and they are a lot older. My theory is that maybe the people that ship these shoes for amazon leave them in a factory that the glue doesn't stay bonded with because of the temperature? I don't know. All I did was take box cutters and cut the sole where it was coming off, now they are good. Anyway these shoes are awesome when the leather softens up and mold to your feet. I wore my first pair to Manhattan to break them in. So my advice is even though they are cheaper on amazon go to a store to buy them to see how good the sole looks. You can tell between a sole that looks like it will stay for a very long time and one that will peel off with the first step. Good luck.

title: UPDATE: Love this shoe!
body:
Hate to give this shoe a 3 star rating as I loved it at first. So much so that I ordered a second pair from another vendor the day after these arrived. First walk was fine. Great support. Second and third walk I had pain in my right foot that felt like when you step on one of your kids's toys really hard. I did notice that there was some extra fabric at the last set of eyelets (very first pair at bottom) on the right shoe and it caused a odd bunching effect on the right shoe when I tightened the laces. Left shoe was perfectly fine. Not sure if this was the cause of the pain, causing the foot to push/roll awkward. I really hope so because if not I'll be stuck with the second pair as I can't return them.

The shoes feel really supportive and I love the fit. The first trial walk was excellent and it continued to be excellent on the left shoe with the middle foot pain being isolated to the right shoe. I returned to a older pair of gel Nimbus 18's and the pain is subsiding significantly. I'll just have to duct tape over the holes in the heels until the other pair arrives. Amazon customer service was excellent and I will return and update this review if the second pair end up being more favorable and pain free. Still a great shoe IMO, may have just gotten a dud.

UPDATE: Shoe was a dud. I have bought a second pair (and even third pair) of these and they fit/feel great. Review updated from 3 to 5 stars. Great shoe!

title: Stylish shoes that have cost me nothing but pain and suffering while hiking
body:
When I first got these boots, I absolutely adored them. To be honest, I still really like the style of them. I've formed an attachment, and as they are so expensive, I kind of have had to just accept that they will be my absurdly expensive around-the-yard and in-town boots. Unfortunately, I got them to be a sturdy boot that I could use for outdoor work and hiking. I got a half-size down as was recommended in many reviews, and while snug, I could get my feet into them...of course this required me unlacing them half the way every time I wanted to put them on. I eventually started only lacing them up to the 2nd to top just so I could get them on a bit faster. They did hurt my feet a bit when I first got them, but I knew that was because they weren't broken in yet. After a week or so, I was hiking in them for a couple hours every few days.

The real horror began once my husband and I got to Ecuador. We are currently spending 2.5 months travelling throughout South America, and we planned on doing A LOT of hiking. A week into our trip, we attempted (but did not finish) the infamous Quilotoa loop. 3 days of long and pretty challenging hikes through the Andes from small town to small town. It was an ideal adventure for avid campers/hikers without a tent. However, on our first day of hiking, my boots began to hurt my feet so bad, I was in tears only 4 hours into our 8 hour trek. When we finally made it to our hostel that night, my entire right ankle (this foot is a bit larger) was raw and bloody. The left ankle was pretty bad too, but not quite as horrible.

Because of this, we couldn't even think of attempting the next day's hike, and instead had to take a cab to the final destination. Once we got there, I slapped some bandaids on my aching ankles and sucked it up to hike down to the lake. I mean, the entire hike was about this, how could I miss it? Unfortunately, this started me limping funny in my boots, rubbing on the side of my right foot more than where it was already injured. Two days later, it became noticeable that the area that had been rubbing more as I avoided further injury, was swelling. Giant, subcutaneous abscesses formed, and within a few days, they were debilitating. I couldn't walk at all.

Being in the Galapagos Islands now, this wasn't exactly an option. I popped pills and stayed in my comfy sandals until finally I couldn't even stand up. Without a proper hospital near, I ended up sterilizing a pin and lancing it myself, finding an abscess nearly half an inch deep. I'll spare you the gorey details, but it took days of repeated draining, and the skin on my ankle still hasn't fully grown back, a month later. Now we're in the Peruvian Andes, in Huaraz, a town known for it's great hikes to stunning glacier lakes...and within just 3 hours of our first hike, I already had nasty blisters that popped and rubbed before we got back to our hotel. This morning we had to entirely call off our hike because it hurts so bad, and it wears on my ankles whether I wear thin socks or thick ones or whether I wrap/bandage the ankle.

So now I am going to buy some cheap shoes in Peru so that I don't have to miss Macchu Picchu, although most of our other significant hikes have already been ruined. All the while, I will be lugging around these useless, beautiful boots, which I probably will never wear if I need to do anymore walking than around a supermarket.

Pretty disappointing experience overall, wish I could say differently, but I can't. These shoes do not hold up to the test of time when it comes to hiking or walking, so unless you're looking to spend a ridiculous amount on leather boots to wear around town, don't even bother.

title: Comfortable, good looking, and stylish!

I get many compliments, and they look nice with winter dresses, leggings and tights. I am prepared for this upcoming humid, snowy winter in the Midwest. I will wear them with 2 socks when temperatures reach single digits or below. I also got the fold down fleece Timberlands half size smaller to wear with tights and thinner socks.
The sole has an awesome grip on wet tile/street/carpeted floors.
You will not want to take them off!

title: How I found the right shoe size for me!
body:
Ok so I knew that based of many online reviews, tarantulace's were the go-to intro climbing shoe. I have some experience with indoor bouldering and top-roping but I've never bit the bullet and bought my own pair. As far as foot shape goes, I would say I have a slightly slim foot, but otherwise all is normal.

In order to get my size exactly, I measured the sole of my foot at the end of a day (to allow for foot swelling). I ended up with a measurement of 42.8cm, so I rounded down to 42.5cm.

I've warn them for about 5 sessions and I love them. They fit snugly and have great traction. I say -1 star because there is a stitch at the heel that can be bothersome at times.

title: Comfy support and flip flops are no longer mutually exclusive concepts!
body:
If you thought you could never wear flip flops because they have no support then think again. I love Vionics for their serious built-in orthotics and these flip flops are true Vionic quality. They stay on my feet, fit snugly and support my feet like no other sandal I've ever worn...that includes my many beloved Merrells along with some Eccos and Keens. My podiatrist suggested Vionics when she fitted me for custom orthotics to address my terribly flat feet and she was right on. Both the fabric toe thong and the foot bed are smooth and comfy. Vionics run a bit large...I typically wear a 5 1/2 in sandals but take a 5 in Vionic sandals. Since Vionics have orthotic support close to custom levels they must be gradually introduced to your feet just as one does with custom orthotics. But once you've done that you will be in love! A side bennie is that these flips look super cute on. I was hesitant to pay this much for flip flops but am I ever glad I did. They are my go to shoe this summer and my feet can't wait to get back into them after wearing Merrells.

Update July 5, 2018: I still adore these flip flops. So much so that I ordered two more pair. Unfortunately neither fit the same as my first pair. I am super disappointed that Vionic needs more work on their quality control. For that price I expect consistency in support and fit. Rating downgraded from five stars to four stars.

title: Great hiking shoe
body:
The Merrell Men's Moab Edge 2 Hiking Shoes are a popular choice for hikers and outdoor enthusiasts looking for a comfortable and durable shoe that can handle a variety of terrains. These shoes feature a breathable mesh upper that allows for plenty of ventilation, helping to keep your feet cool and comfortable even on hot days. The upper also has synthetic overlays that add durability and support to the shoe.

The Moab Edge 2 also features a Vibram® outsole, which provides excellent traction on a variety of surfaces. This outsole is designed to grip well on both wet and dry surfaces, so you can feel confident and secure as you hike over rocky or slippery terrain. The shoe also has a molded nylon arch shank that adds stability and support to the shoe, while a Merrell Air Cushion in the heel provides additional cushioning and shock absorption.

One of the standout features of the Moab Edge 2 is its comfort. The shoe has a breathable mesh lining that helps to keep your feet cool and dry, and the M Select™ FIT.ECO+ blended EVA contoured footbed provides excellent arch support and cushioning. The shoe also has a traditional lace-up closure that allows you to customize the fit, so you can achieve a comfortable and secure fit that's tailored to your foot.

Overall, the Merrell Men's Moab Edge 2 Hiking Shoes are an excellent choice for hikers and outdoor enthusiasts looking for a comfortable and durable shoe that can handle a variety of terrains. With their breathable mesh upper, Vibram® outsole, and comfortable footbed, these shoes are sure to provide you with the support and comfort you need on your next hike.

title: Really solid shoe for working and hiking
body: I needed a comfortable low-cut shoe for yard work and walking/light hiking, and I had had good experience with a Moab hiking boot, but I ordered that boot a half-size larger than my usual 9 M, and the 9.5 M fit perfectly, so I contacted Merrill and asked if I should do the same with this Moab 2 low-cut.  They said yes, so I ordered it for a really good price on Amazon, and it fits very well.  I might have been able to get away with ordering a 9 M in this shoe, but the 9.5 M fits well with plenty of room in the toe box but no sloppiness in the support.  An added bonus is that these are fairly light, though a lot heavier than running shoes, very sturdy and stable, and, so far, waterproof.  I have done some morning outdoor work in heavy dew without any wetness getting inside.  These shoes are also fairly breathable.  All in all, an excellent buy.

title: Nearly perfect, but for a couple of small factors.
body: I was on a mission to find the "perfect" shoe. I needed something that would stand up to a lot of abuse in unforgiving environments. I specifically did not want a waterproof shoe as I needed excellent breathability due to frequent extended wear (>24hr at a time). Something tough as nails but comfortable enough for intercontinental flights. I looked closely at dozens of different shoes from every vendor in this space. Bought  around 5 or 6 different ones (thanks Amazon try before you buy). This shoe was hands down the best in all categories. Super comfortable. Breathable and cool in even the most uncomfortable climate and the longest of extended wear. Incredibly tough and confidence inspiring in the roughest environment. The only thing I don't care for is the loop lace eyelets. They will wear out before anything else on the shoes. I wish standard grommet eyelets were used, but I'm willing to live with it and just go easy on lace ups. You won't be disappointed in this shoe. Note: It runs about a half-size small (order a half-size larger than you normally would).

The plasticy skin of the shoe started cracking and the heel started separating after a single day of hiking. After a few weeks of fairly mild use, the shoes were still comfortable but not remotely waterproof. Stepping in even a small amount of standing water or mud would go straight into the bottom of the shoe.

If you purchase these shoes, it's apparently quite a cr@pshoot as to whether you'll get a pair that last or fall apart immediately.

The fit was great and the shoes are still comfortable. I just can't wear them off of sidewalks. Even wet grass results in a wet foot.

title: Fantastic comfort fit for a beginner with wide feet.
body:
My first pair, so Ill keep it brief as Im probably not the best person to do an in depth analysis.

I have wide feet. Like... WIDE... and the whole time I was demo-ing different shoes I was afraid that I'd be squished into a pair thats just too damn tight because you're not supposed to have any toe wiggle room in climbing shoes. Well, this pair liberated me from all of those worries. I tried a bunch of high end pairs by Scapra and its nothing against them, but this was the first and pretty much only pair that I could wear for 40+ minutes without serious discomfort, to the point where towards the end I forgot I even had them on. Super comfortable on any indoor climbs, the lacing is legit and easy to tighten/loosen, there is a slight bend curve to the shape which helps me prioritize the toe when climbing (as a beginner)... I dont even know what else to comment on. For me comfort was the biggest worry point and these shoes totally put me at ease.

UPDATE: Well, its July 2017 and since this review helped a bunch of people out heres a followup:

What the shoes have put up with since the original review:
- A good amount of bouldering
- Me working my way from 5.6's to 5.11's (indoor only)
- A TON of bad smearing, questionable foot flagging, and general flailing around to compensate for bad technique as I was learning.

Overall experience:
- Fit has been fantastic. No pain points, no tight spots, I can wear these for hours without taking them off and not feel any discomfort
- Barely any stretching. Laces held up, easy to put on and off
- Don't smell. Im not a '7 hours out door' climber yet, but I haven't done a single thing to de-odor them since I've had them, and they're still fine
- Durable, as evident from the stuff I put them through

Final word:
Do the toes fit like a high end aggressive shoe? Nope. Is there a little bit of room in the heel making some heel holds sketchy? Occasionally. Despite that were they worth the hours of comfort, reducing one more thing I had to worry about as a beginner and letting me focus on technique and training without making my feet hurt? Absolutely. I've finally wore through the toe on these no doubt due to bad technique, and if it wasn't for sheer curiosity about how some of the other shoes fit/differ, I'd hands down get these again.

title: La Sportiva Tarantulace
body:
Got this shoe because I had originally ordered a pair of Evolv Geshidos, and they were way too uncomfortable for a new climber.

These are a great value and very good shoe for a beginner, and will probably last a long time. I prefer lace-ups because I have a wide foot and enjoy the added versatility of the lacing. Good grip, good edging, very comfortable, all-around good shoe. These aren't as aggressive as your top of the line rock shoe, but they are perfect for the gym, which is where I use them.

As people warn, they run large. I'm a European size 43, and I got a 41.5. After I broke them in I was wishing I'd ordered the 41. Get at least 1.5 sizes smaller, maybe even 2. The leather will stretch out after about a week of climbing and then these will fit like a glove.

title: Satisfaction found.
body:
Let's get the basics out of the way:
My size shoe is 12 or 12.5 USA depending on brand. I can do an 11.5 wide comfortably too.
I purchased my pair from Recreational Equipment and was able to use a coupon to save 10 bucks.(I still think the shoes are a great value at the current price of $80)
I am a beginner, both in terms of invested time, and experience with gear. Other than the shoes, I only own what I needed to buy to avoid gear rental fees. (Harness, shoes, carabiner, belay device)

Now on to the review!
Fit: I tried them on in a store. The Tarantulace was the only shoe model the store had in my size that fit. I had to adjust the lacing, and my feet are a bit wider than the sole. A fit is a fit though, and this pair won out by default there. After ownership, I'm happy to say that the shoes still fit and I'm not regretting it with discomfort.

Fit is perfect.

Style: eh. Wish they were in blue. They didnt stain my feet after 3 hours of wearing them, but I sorta wanted to look like the hulk below the ankle.

Comfort: they fit. Doesn't sound like much, but fit and comfort go hand in hand. My toe didn't feel crunched in. My sole didn't feel much discomfort due to being wider than the sole.

Performance: as someone new to the shoes with no frame of reference beside rentals, they work. If they last, or I get to try another pair, I can be more helpful here. So far so good for now.

title: Excellent beginners / moderate climbing shoes
body:
I gave it 5 stars because the shoes are of great quality. I have wore them consistently for all my climbs during the pass few months. Since it uses laces and not Velcro, it wraps around your feet like a glove.
Few things to keep in consideration:
1) La Sportiva climbing shoes are usually narrower than most other brand. ( I have narrow feet)
2) I consider the shoes for beginners and intermediate because the arc is not too high.
3) They are supposed to be used without socks; therefore, use some type of powder or spray (Dr. Scholls) and let them freshen out to keep them dry and without smell.
4) the size should be (US) 1 less than your regular Snickers. If you wear Adidas or Nike running shoes size 10, then this shoes should be 9
I would recommend this shoes to anyone climbing in an indoor gym at any level of expertise, or for beginners and intermediate climbers. If you are an advance climber that climbs outside on real rock, then a harder more arched shoe is recommended.

title: Solid shoes
body: So far I've used these in the gym both top roping and bouldering and haven't had any issues with discomfort or performance. They work great, but the break in period was painful and took a few sessions to get them fully acclimated to my feet but they've been a pleasure to climb in ever since. I wear a 10.5 naturally and decided to go with a 10 in these as people suggest getting a size or so smaller than your normal size. I only wish I got the velcro version, but nonetheless a great purchase and I recommend these shoes if you are starting out.

title: Must break in before enjoying
body:
This is my second pair of rainbows. I had the same exact pair before for two years. I wore them all of the time and they probably looked half their age. They wear nicely in terms of how well they look even after being worn for years. Unfortunately, my dog thought they might be a great snack. Womp womp... $50 later I secured my second pair.

The worst part about rainbows is that they take a while to break in. I bought my first pair right before a vacation to hawaii. Unfortunately, I wore them only a few times in two weeks because the first time was so painful. When my first pair was destroyed, I was more upset about having to break in a second pair than I was about having to fork over the money for another pair. When they arrived, I started wearing them around the house like slippers and then gradually took them out of the house for longer and longer stretches. Once they are broken in, they will immediately become your favorite, most comfortable, go-to pair of flip flops. It is worth the time investment. (and financial investment too for that matter)

The pair shown here is about 3 months old, with daily use.

title: Sketchers designs awesome shoes!
body:
These are extremely light weight and comfortable shoes. Like walking on air. If you just look at this shoe it has the appearance of having bulky, heavy materials, stiff & hard to wear. This is so NOT what these shoes are. The memory foam makes these very cushiony to wear. The over all weight of the shoe is light. They are constructed really well, NO falling apart, separating at seams, coming unglued from stepping in water. I need comfy shoes for arthritic knees and body and these really make shopping & walking, an easy task. No achy or painful knees, ankles, legs after wearing them all day.
I also love the roomy wide toe area. Excellent arch support, and beautiful design/style. And they sure don't look like "grandma shoes".

title: Comfortable for wide feet
body: Rain boots are almost a daily requirement where I live so I was looking for a boot that was not only rugged and durable but also comfortable and fashionable.  I normally wear a 7.5 - 8 wide width and I have fairly large calves.  Most boots that I had tried on (Bogs, Muck, XtraTuf, etc) were either too tall, way too tight in the calf, or very tight around my foot.  I ordered an 8 in these boots and I find that they do fit true to size but since I have wide feet I can only wear them with thin socks.  My feet can get fairly cold in them so I think I'll order a 9 next time in the hopes that I'll be able to wear them with wool socks or a liner.  What I love about these boots is that they look great while hiking in the forest or running errands in town and they are comfortable enough to wear for hours.  I also love that the inside of the boots is soft....almost silky.  It doesn't pill up or fall apart like the cheap felt lining of some other boots and it isn't just straight rubber (like the outside of the boot) so it allows my foot to breathe and not get too sweaty.  I'll definitely reorder another pair when these ones finally wear out.....I'll just order a size up.

title: Lightweight, cushioned run
body:
These shoes felt good to walk in and great to run in. They are lightweight but offer a lot of cushioning to protect your knees. I felt a bounce in my step and ran my usual loop at a bit faster pace.

I like how much the top of the shoe opens up while the tongue has its own control so it's not flopping around or getting misshapen. The black with blue highlights is also cool but subtle.

The only downside that I have noticed is that it rained the night before and I could feel the shoe slipping on the blacktop for a few strides after running through a wet area. If the whole paved trail was wet, it would have been annoying or even painful.

I wear an 11.5 or a 12, depending on the brand, and a 12 was perfect for the Ride Iso 2.

Update after a month and a half of running 2-4 miles most day: Docking a star in the review as one shoes has developed a hole on the inside heel. These shoes do a good job of holding onto your foot, so I hoped that tightness would prevent my foot from slipping around and wearing this hole.

title: Not durable at all

title: This boot pronates
body: I am a long-time Keen user from work boots to walking shoes to basic camping/hiking boots.  I tried two of the same size Targhee's and each one has a pronounced pronating stance - it leans your ankles and knees inward towards each other.  It dod not feel like a neutral natural stance when standing still and was an issue on just a short hike.  Both were returned.  I run and use a neutral low cushioned shoe that allows the leg geometry to function which matters if you are in a shoe/boot for any length of time especially on uneven terrain.  Traded them in for the Keen Gypsum II and what a difference for my size 13 feet.  If the sole design on this does not suit you, consider the Gypsum which based on two attempts at the Targhee III, is a much more natural sole and walking motion.

title: Great Support, Durable, Comfortable and True to Size.
body: While they are not the most inexpensive boots out there, they have the support, comfort and overall design of pricier boots. I've had many mid and lightweight hikers, and there are probably the best.  They are durably constructed with a thoughtful lacing design that facilitates support.  The body, mid sole and curved last are all sturdy but still flexible - with most boots in this category you often sacrifice flexibility for sturdiness, or vice versa.  They are also true to size, which is a plus.

title: Super comfortable

I haven’t used them for hiking but I’ve used them clearing brush, building a deck, pressure washing driveways, they clean up easily. I wear size 12 medium in tennis shoes and the keen fit true to size for me.

title: The tongues won't stay centered on my ankles
body: I like Keen boots because they are comfortable to wear. However, I bought a pair of the Keen Targhee III boots about a year ago and the tongues on both boots slip to the outside of my feet after an hour or more of wear. The laces and edges of the tongues start digging into my ankles and I have to stop and reposition the tongues - which fixes the problem for a short while and then it repeats. I'm curious if anyone else has this problem or maybe I just received an aberrant pair??

title: Best shoes for pronated feet. Fits true to size
body: My 2 year old son has over pronated feet and we were looking for a supportive sneaker to try and correct them. These shoes quickly became my sons favorite sneakers, and although we saw some improvement after a month or so, we made an appointment with a foot and ankle doctor to get a professional opinion and my son wore these to the appointment. The doctor was impressed with these sneakers and admitted he didn’t know about this version (v5). He normally recommends a different New Balance 990 shoe to parents (v3) but thought these were better because of the overall quality and the velcro option for small kids. He said the main things you want to look for in a sneaker for pronated feet are good arch support, a thick heel, strong ankle support, and wide toe width. I included a picture for reference. Although these shoes are very supportive and can often correct mild cases of pronation, my son needed custom-made orthotics (which fit perfect in these shoes with the original inserts removed). My son wears size a size 8 in all shoes and these fit true to size. I hope my review is helpful for others considering purchasing.

title: From a Former Runner
body: Four years ago, my "last" pair of running shoes was the Wave Runner 12.  It/they replaced a lifetime series of Asics Gel Cumulus purchases. And I could run, with a 3:00 marathon, 1:23 half, and 36:11 10K back in the day.  I liked the Wave Runner, but my left knee was on the way out.  So it/they served me through the last three months of running, a knee replacement, a knee infection & knee fusion, and a "revision."  Needless to say, I'm lucky to be walking these days but had to replace the worn-out 12s.  The 24 is comfy for walking though I'd rather be able to shuffle/jog, but that won't happen again.  Still, I can walk (slowly) and dream.  I do like the reflective trim on the outside of the sole for early-morning visibility.  Toe box is comfy & fabric forgiving.  Heel height a tad higher than I'd design but OK.  Shoe laces not as high quality as in the old days.  But it is nice to have an operative new pair.

title: Soft Enough To Feel Like Running Barefoot
body: These shoes are meant for running and are designed for a a lower impact hit.  They have a good strike and support flexing.  The padding inside is simply some of the most comfortable I have felt outside of installed aftermarket orthotics.  The sole cushions the footfalls such that you really feel comfortable with medium distance (>5 mi) running.  If you find this to be a good shoe, I would buy a couple of pairs, because this model has design changes from year-to-year.

title: Questionable quality on this generation.  Mizuno honors warranty, though +UPDATE+
body:
These shoes are so comfortable and were exactly what I wanted. Fit my feet well, had a decent upper that doesn't pinch the top of my feet and a comfortable toe box. I like they way they hit the ground when running and they really feel natural. Whoever *designed* the shoe should get a high-5.

The shoes are manufactured horribly. Just like multiple reviews state, the uppers are tearing, the outsole's glue is failing on the tread and I'm tripping over the treads as they break from their glue.

I weigh 170lb and have ran 47 miles in these shoes since purchased 6 weeks prior to this review.

I would like to say that I emailed Mizuno USA and they honored the shoe warranty immediately. The company will keep my business for now, and I'll just hope they make some adjustments for the Wave Rider 25

**UPDATE --It has been about 4 weeks since my replacements have arrived and I just noticed the same defect is starting to form in the replacement pair. Maybe I have weird feet because otherwise i'd expect to see more of a similar complaint.
