ORIGINAL: This shoe is awesome. I have two small gripes with it. The fabric in the toe has become indented such that on one toe there is an inward lump that brushes against my toes. This happened while hiking and it went from annoying to potentially blister-causing. The other issue is that there is a large groove running through the sole of the shoe and that can get large rocks stuck in it fairly easily. Otherwise these are great, super comfortable, and supportive. Certainly would buy again despite these issues.

I would recommend this shoe I'm really nervous when it comes to buying shoes online but I purchase like several pairs of shoes call 10 and 1/2 and they all fit me good. Except for this shoe it doesn't seem to be measuring at the same other shoe companies that seem to be out there I don't understand how all these shoe companies cannot get the sizes right because. I weigh 200 lbs and my foot already rolls too much to the outside; so I bought a shoe with "stability" (Asics GT-2000 -8) to keep my forefoot flat.

title: Forrest would like these :)
body:
Updated Jan 2021:
Same issue as the WaveRider 23... the inside left heel fabric tore open. There’s something going on with the heel flex point and the hard plastic “heel cup” where the fabric catches and tears. 😏 this hopefully gets reinforced/ fixed on the next gen design. I untie and loosen laces - so it’s not from me forcing my foot into the shoe.

= = = = = = =
Brand new to me this week. First couple runs = same perfect fit. I noticed these are a touch more narrow than previous models, but still a generous toe box with good flexibility... no rub spots. They feel good - as they should. Laces are short if you tie them with the back eyelet like I do - but that’s trivial. 5-star in my book. I’ll update this after additional mileage.

title: Don’t wear very well

This pair of Wave Rider 24’s has only 70 miles on them and are already showing significant wear. As far as comfort.. they are no better or worse than the 23’s… regardless what the professional reviewers say. I will not buy another pair of these shoes.. and I have had over 15 pair of Mizunos’s.
Edit: Just ordered a pair of Wave Rider 23's as the 24's have worn out after only 150 miles... poor design from Mizuno. If they keep this up, I will certainly be switching brands

title: Mizuno running shoes for the win!
body:
[[VIDEOID:69cfcccd2b31bfa8aed8273d23f00159]] So, I picked these shoes up with a few others to do a review video and compare their initial fit and comfort. I had never tried Mizuno before, and to be honest I thought they were just a baseball equipment company.

Imagine my shock when they turned out to be one of the most comfortable shoes out of the whole review. These shoes are lightweight but still felt sturdy and solid when wearing them. The soles have a nice curve to them, which almost gives the feeling of being propelled forward when moving.

The support around the ankle was great, and the length and fit were on the nose based on my typical shoe size.

I did an unboxing and full video review of these (and a few other brands) on my recent YouTube video, search Fizzness Shizzness to check it out

title: Mizuno Waves
body:
I really wanted to put these shoes to the test this past weekend on some strenuous runs and hikes due to their price but, I can honestly say that these Mizuno’s are well worth the price.

I will first say that they fit to exact size. They are a bit snug, so, if you’re unsure of getting a wide setting - I would recommend doing so as the outline is very slim and form fitting. The shoes offer incredible support while also giving a nice bouncy cushion for super stressful runs and high impact workouts. These waves are also very attractive and have a wonderful sporty feel to their aesthetic. Overall, I’m very satisfied with its performance and appearance.

I would definitely recommend these runners.

title: Gorgeous boot!
body:
I'm a huge fan of Blundstones! I have another pair that fits like a glove after more than 5 years of wear.. they just get more comfy.
I really like the style of this pair, so I bought them in antique brown. Like others, I had trouble with sizing. As others suggested, I first tried a half size up (size 10.5) even though my other blundstone pair are size 10. I found them to be a little too loose, and I prefer my shoes snug so I sized back down to my regular 10. They fit snug and can be tight with really big socks, but I'd prefer to start snug and stretch them out than have boots get more and more roomy-- especially with the heal. Others have mentioned that they are SO HARD to get off (and on)... but I suspect this problem will ease a bit with time since they are leather :)
I highly recommend this boot!! One thing to note is that these shoes are not super warm in cold winter weather. I wear my blundstones in winter a lot despite this, and my toes freeze pretty quickly even with big socks. It's because they're not super insulated .

title: Can't quite decide what I think about these yet

I sized up a half size in part because of the recommendations and in part because my usual size (7.5) was sold out. The 8 seems to fit fine with a medium weight sock, so I assume 8.5 would have been too big, but 7.5 may have also fit because the 8 is not snug. I've since read that you shouldn't size up because of the way Blundstones stretch and mold to your foot. I do like to wear boots with thick socks so I expect if these stretch I'll wear a thicker sock and it will be fine.

Pros: I like the look of the boots when I look down at them on my feet. The Antique Taupe is a bit lighter than my other leather boots, but it looks great with blue or black jeans and it's cute with black leggings. The look is versatile and would look good dressed up or down.

Cons: arrived with minimal packing materials inside the box and had several scratches and some slight areas of discoloration like they had been in a store before being sold at Amazon. Also the ankle shaft seems to slope forward, which makes the heel area of the boot look huge. I'm hoping that might kind of stretch or something over time, however I have skinny ankles so it may not.

title: Finally, Blundstone's for women with long skinny feet
body:
These (mine are the dark brown 1673's) look and feel great on my long skinny feet. Not gonna lie -- that wasn't my take when I first put them on. They seemed way too wide and long. I always wear a Euro size 39, which in these is a size 9 (usually a 8.5 in US shoe sizing). But I know I always have to customize because I have such narrow feet. Into these, I put an extra thick Dr. Scholl's foam insole, and on top of that an orthotic type of insole that has a subsnatial arch. These help hold the food in place and keep them from sliding forward. Then, I selected one of the heaviest pairs of socks from my vast sock inventory. After all that, they fit exactly as I wish -- snug around the foot, enough length for the toes.

But as for "what do you most want to know"-- it has to be said, what I often most want to know is whether a pair of boots is going to emphasize just how long my feet are. A size 39 is a pretty big boot for someone who is just 5'2" so any pair that I seriously consider has to at least not make the issue any worse than it is. These perform quite well in that department -- even in the brown color (a departure from my habitual black).

For me, with my skinny ankles and calves, the narrow openings are just right. I had no problem at all putting them on or taking them off, using the pull tabs. You feel them around your legs, but even over pushed-down heavy socks, it is not a problem for me.

The brown of the 1673 is just as pictured in the photos. I wanted them a little darker -- some AppleCare leather lotion too care of that nicely.

The one reservation I have about these is: how do you renew the heels and soles? But I guess I will worry about that when the time comes, if it comes, and perhaps just buy a new pair.

The sneaker that came was rather wide and loose. I checked the label to see if I had been sent a wide shoe by mistake, but it had not. Apparently the normal shoe is too wide for the normal foot. I am just going to keep it to be used occasionally, but next time, I am going to shop for a sneaker at a brick and mortar store, so I can physically try it out for size. JC Penny could use my business. I always liked that store.

Update: It was just too uncomfortably wide...and I returned it. Amazon gave me a prompt refund.

One issue I also noticed was that the rise in the back had the potential to rub against my ankle bone where the Fibula meets the foot. I purchased another pair online last year and did not discover this until I wore them on the treadmill at the gym and then it was too late to return them. These were asics but very low quality as to what I am used to seeing from Asics.  So I am now going to see if I can find a higher end shoe to meet my needs.

title: Worth every penny. These are the best shoes I've ever owned.
body: My wife always says you can save money on a lot of things, but when it comes to shoes, don't skimp. With shoes, you generally get what you pay for. Very true in this case. The first day I ever wore these I had to spend a marathon workday in our state capital during the state legislative session. Most of the day I was on my feet. I put these shoes on in the morning, wore them for 13 hours straight, up and down stairs, to and from a lunch meeting and other meetings, on city sidewalks, to and from and through an evening reception, etc., and I never once thought of my feet (other than looking down to admire how damn nice these shoes looked). I can't believe how comfortable they are. If you have to look nice for work or throw on a suit every now and again, I can't recommend these shoes highly enough.

title: These Are Factory 2nds

I have no doubt they are the authentic shoe, however when these arrived they had scratches on the uppers, the welt stitching was slightly loose, and the insole had scratches on it. title: Disappointed
body:
This is my first pair of AE so for the price of $259 I expected a very nice shoe. I should add, even if these were 2nd's I didn't expect the type if issues I encountered.

1st pair - Took out of the box and the right shoe looked fine so I was rather pleased and excited. I took the left shoe out and I cringed. The cap toe was certainly not 180 degrees across but looked majorly crooked and easily noticeable. Also to add the heel on the left shoe was much longer than the one on the right shoe when putting the two shoes together, not a huge deal but the crooked left shoe is a big enough deal to return.

2nd pair - Same situation as the 1st pair. The right shoe looked perfect but the left shoe is crooked even worst than the first pair. At this point I feel like the $259 surely isn't worth it for a pair of shoes that don't match unless my right foot is straight and I always have my left foot pointed outwards so the shoe looks straight.

I ended up trying the shoes out for a day to see if they were as comfortable as I've heard. I wore them for a couple hours and I've found that these are pretty narrow even with getting a 13E. Needless to say, even after getting past the defects, I'm going to have to return as these just aren't wide enough for my foot.

If you look at picture you will notice something missing...Shoelaces.  Also, notice the broguing.  The Park Avenue model shown in the picture on the site  is a Cap Toe, with NO broguing.  Lastly, my previous shoes came in an Allen Edmunds shoebox, and cloth shoe bags.  These shoes were just wrapped in tissue paper, loose inside the shipping box.  When you spend $400+ on a pair of shoes, you expect the correct model, shoelaces, and better packaging..SMH

You are better off trying them on at a store before you commit so much money to a pair of shoes.

title: Disappointed
body: I finally went out and got some "nice" shoes. They do look great, which is why they are getting two stars instead of one. If they were $100 cheaper, I'd have given them three stars based on appearance alone. Problem is, they hurt my feet. At first I thought it was just that I had an ill-fitting pair of shoes but something is different about these. Eventually I figured it out. My feet fit fine in them until I walk around. The problem is that the leather is hard and unforgiving as are the soles. I've worn them for about 20 hours in two consecutive work days, maybe as they break in the fit will improve but I shouldn't have to "break in" shoes that were this expensive before I can walk around without pain. Buying them was a mistake.

title: Shoes arrived obviously worn, but otherwise high quality.
body:
Was very excited to receive these shoes in the mail (Nicest shoes I've ever bought, will be wearing them to my wedding) and was looking forward to the whole unboxing. Black box with gold type, flannel shoe bags, pristine leather, the whole luxury experience.

Was however disappointed to receive a fairly dinged up box, and shoes that had very obviously been worn on rough terrain. The soles already had deep scratches in the leather, as if someone had tried them on by walking on gravel or rough asphalt, and there were some deep grooves on the insoles which I can't figure out the possible cause of.

I will be keeping them anyways, as the scuffing will be quickly outdone by a single wear, and the upper leather is still in perfect condition condition. Plus I paid $280 on Amazon vs $425 from the Allen Edmonds store, so some sole scuffs are worth the discount in my opinion. Still, for a luxury product it is unfortunate to have such obvious wear right from the box, and if I were buying these as a gift for someone I would have to return them for a pristine pair.

Besides that they actually came in a box (not an AE box)that was to big  with 1 piece of paper in there for protection.The box is big enough to put another pair of shoes in there.So these shoes also have the scuffs and scratches you would expect from being beaten up and thrown around inside the  box .

title: Very high-quality, classic leather-soled shoes

They seem to fit most closely to the Park Ave, which is a very similar design. I wear the Park Aves on average about once per week or so, and they have held up very well in the 6 months I've owned them. I have worn them with a suit on several occasions. You really can't go wrong with these.

I am unable to tell about the right one at this time, as I am unable to lace it up.  Seems as though one end of the shoe lace didn't get the plastic tip thing it needs to go through the lace holes.  I am hoping this review will inform Amazon of the issue, and they can just send me an extra matching shoe lace without me having to exchange the whole order.

body:
I was really looking forward to have a pair of Allen Edmonds. Good reviews and good name brand.

Since I already wore them, I can't send them back. I took it to a shoe place for a shine, and they pointed out the almost unnoticeable lines on the right shoe. He said it was due to the leather not matching and that I will experience uneven wear due to the lower quality of (or maybe defective) leather on one shoe.

Very disappointing due to the price and reputation of these shoes. I did pay less than the retail of $399 here at Amazon, but are these supposed to be the "B" stock? If so, I'm not aware of it. The shine of the shoes are matching now, but if you look at them closely, you'll still see the lines on the right shoe.

title: Be prepared to exchange
body:
Please do not buy these shoes unless you are comfortable with less than first quality. These are NOT second quality shoes from AE but they are not first quality. I have owned quite a few AE's and these do not have the second quality marking but they are not first quality.

I bought these because my old ones were wore out and I have a business trip to NY next week and needed some quickly. (Prime) That was a mistake. The first pair had a defect in the captoe with the leather being sowed in wrong. The second pair had stitching mistakes all over the shoe. I know these are hand stitched so I understand there may be some small imperfections, but these were highly noticeable.

Returns were easy and they exchanged the shoes but by now I could have ordered them from the factory. Not saying you will get a bad shoe but I would be prepared to make a few exchanges.

title: Another Great Wallabee
body:
I needed to replace my HUGELY ADORED old pair of Wallabees due to 6 years of wear, so I ordered these. They're just a bit different in that there's a loop in back but no traditional Wallabee crepe-rubber sole. Here it's a Vibram sole attached to a leather midsole: a somewhat less comfy arrangement than the directly-applied crepe of the original design, but a great update because the added midsole allows for replacing the Vibram soles underneath when they're past it.
The blue color features nubuck leather on top & suede on the sides, but be cautious with the black because it actually has FUR on top! That's a faux calf hair from what I read elsewhere - but still rather weird to see if you overlooked that aspect while looking at the pics online. In either case, the Wallabee Hike is a good-quality variation of a truly great chukka boot. Research suede care so that you can properly maintain the uppers of these shoes, & they should serve you very well for many years to come.

I walked around the house a bit to test them out and no matter how I tied the laces, no matter what socks I wore, I could NOT keep my heel from slipping out of the back of the shoe.  I have a pretty average shaped foot (not particularly narrow or wide in any areas), and have never had a shoe fit me like this.  The only time my heel has ever slipped out of a shoe in the past was when the shoe was a size too big - and in those cases, the shoe was too big all over.  This shoe fit me fairly okay everywhere else EXCEPT the heel.  It's really too bad, because the style of the shoe is very cute.

title: I so like this shoe.
body:
I purchased this in Beeswax color, size 11M. I have other shoes made by Clarks but have never owned or really looked into the Wallabee shoe. After musing over this shoe for a few weeks, I decided to give the Wallabee II's at a try instead of the first edition. The difference is the Wallabee has a crepe sole, while the Wallabee II has a rubber composite sole (firm and longer lasting.) While I do love crepe soles, I live in Georgia and it gets pretty hot, especially the sidewalks. Extreme heat and water are not good for crepe soles in my opinion, so, I prefer to wear crepe soles anytime outside of the summer months and non-rainy days. I like the new rubber composite sole because it is better at resisting the extreme heat temperatures in the south. In essence, I can wear the Wallabee II's all year around. I rotate shoes, so I expect these to last a while, as all others have, to include my crepe soles. These shoes were comfortable to me right out of the box. I prefer a wedge sole in this type of shoe because there is no need for a shank. I have severe back problems, so a stable shoe is must for me, as well as comfort. This is my second pair of Clarks (different shoe) Beeswax color and I like it a lot. This particular color can be used with a wide variety of colors, I would say more so than a black pair, or which I will purchase later, lol. This look is not for everyone, but it is for me. Simple, quality, reasonably priced. I'm all in. Some shoes require that I use a special orthopedic insert, but this is not the case with the Wallabee II thus far.

I purchased these through Amazon, but the ordered was fulfilled by Peltz Shoes out of NY. This is my first purchase from this vendor. Shipping was free, but not Prime, and it arrived earlier than expected. So, quick shipping, less than a week. My product arrived in new condition and according to what I specified. I would recommend this vendor, and I will do future business with them. I would rate Peltz Shoes as a 5-star experience. I have not made contact with the vendor directly, but I am totally satisfied with their services and products thus far. I so like this shoe!

title: boots are crap
body:
My last pair of Doc Martens 1460 lasted for 6 years of heavy work. I wear them as barn boots and hiking boots. They always kept my feet comfortable and dry.

After 6 years, the leather started to crack and I needed a new pair. I did a "REORDER", rather than browse to find them. This boot is what was selected. It is NOT the same. If the original boot is nolonger available, Amazon should have so stated.

I wore the new boots today for the first time. The grass was wet. The water soaked right through the leather. My socks were soaked within minutes.

I would return the boots if I could. But since I wore them once, the return policy does not allow me to return them.

If you want the boots only for fashion use, by all means, get these boots.

title: Worth the Price!!!
body: I got the monochrome smooth black boots for work. I work in a lab with frozen specimens. I spend quite some time in a walk in freezer and the slip proof sole is invaluable for this. They are pretty tough boots but more comfortable than alot of shoes i've worn. Even a pair of Dr. Scholl's brand shoes didn't compare to these. After walking around for eight hours at work, my feet feel golden. The title said women's boots at amazon but these are pretty much unisex at other places. I usually wear an US 8 1/2 and i tried on a 9 at a store and it was too big so i sized down to a US 8 (UK 7)when i ordered from amazon. The size was dead-on on my foot. I was a little worried at first but they stretched out to a perfect fit over a week of daily wear. Do wear thick socks or put bandages where the boot rubs because it will rub you raw. Do this until they mold to your feel (about a week). The back of the ankle was the worst spot for me so i put fabric bandaids on in those spots before i put the boots on. The ones i received were made in thailand for those who care - I don't!!! They are awesome quality boots. If you polish them with shoe wax they will get really shiny or just clean them and keep them with that "smooth" look.

title: I use these shoes for racquetball and they're pretty good
body:
Bought these shoes specifically for use during racquetball. This is the second pair that I've bought. It's just super hard to find good athletic shoes for playing racquetball. For the price, they're hard to beat.
I play raquetball two days a week, and for 2 hours each day, so I put these shoes through their paces and got about 1.5 years out of them. I'm actually surprised they lasted as long as they did. Their grip on the polished hardwood floor is great and with all the side-side movement I never injured an ankle.
Regarding the comfort and sizing. I wear a size 9.5 EEE so it's always nice to find a good shoe with the correct width. These shoes fit that 9.5 EEE perfectly. Not too big or short, and just the right width. It does take about 3-4 weeks of racquetball to break them in, though. Until then they aren't quite as comfortable on the court and my feet are a little sore at the end of the matches.
Highly recommend these shoes.

title: THEY RUN SMALL!
body:
I ordered a size 9.5. I'm usually in a 9.5 to 10

I even measured my foot using the tracing method. Length is about 10.5" width is 4" and that's being generous.

Converting 10.5 inch to cm is 26.7CM I rounded up (again, being generous).
I literally went to their website and looked at their sizing guide. It says a 9 would be the size to get.
So I figure, ok well I'm usually about a 9.5 to 10 so I'll get the 9.5

My toe is literally at the VERY tip of the shoe.
They feel super narrow and cramped. I definitely feel like I need to go a whole size, not just a half size, up to 10.5, and maybe even to a 2E wide.

its possible it will wear in, but I don't want that. I'm buying new shoes to be a bit more spacious and comfortable, not to be some hammer-toe pain inducing torture device.

New Balance, you NEED to post a proper sizing guide on the product page. This is unacceptable. I'll be returning these.

Other than the sizing they overall feel like decent shoes. 85$ worth? well I don't know about that. Depends on how they last but I'll need to order another pair that actually fits.

title: Half size down, quality control and great style.
body:
First, my good thoughts. Love the style of the boot. The leather texture feels really nice and I like the build of the boot. Has the right amount of bulk to it, and the right amount of space for thicker socks, if you need to wear them. My girlfriend really likes how the boots look on me.

The not-so-exciting thoughts. The leather material of the boot does change after a few wearings. The front and back hold on to that rich leather color, but the middle changes to a worn-out look. Not a bad thing for me since I like that look. I normally wear a size 11 US but had to go down a size, to 10.5 US with these boots. You might want to consider a flat insole if you need more of a cushioned feel. And the last thing. For the price of the boot and after less than a week of owning these, I was surprised the shoelace ring came off the top of one of the boots. (pictured) I'm taking it to a shoe repair shop to get fixed, and hopefully, they will either use the same ring or come up with a better solution.

Update: Got the shoe ring fixed and they've been solid since. So far, I've been happy after they've broken in and hope I get a lot of years out of them.

title: Brok-in just to have them brok-en
body:
Yes, you're putting my words together right. Let's start with what's good first:
-High quality tread and threads on leather.
-Seems to be water-proof
-Decent leather; nice color
-Great price...

What's been bad:
-Integrity issue. Broken lace loop at ankle top; just pulled the metal right out as I was tightening the laces— what it's supposed to be designed for, it failed. Other reviewers also complain about this happening to them. It will likely happen on your pair, too.
-Now I must get them repaired; likely to cost me more money and time.
-...Great price —beware, you get what you paid for.
- Leather scratches up easily.

title: Good sneaker/winter boot combo
body: I purchased these because winter boots were causing pain and blisters from 2-3 mile dog walks and my feet weren’t warm enough in my regular running shoes.  These are waterproof, warm and supportive.  I sized up, as I do with running shoes, so my toes weren’t hitting the end and so I could wear thick socks.  Admittedly, I was concerned about the bulky sole that many complained about.  The heel has hit stair treads, but I’m really only wearing them outside, so it is a non-issue for me.  The only time these won’t be my go-to is when the snow is over 6” or so, but that doesn’t happen much anymore.  They may not always be the most stylish choice, but Sorel makes great quality footwear, especially for the cooler months.  You definitely get your money’s worth!

title: Amazon's size recommendation was spot on
body:
My shoe size is somewhere between an 8 and 8 1/2, but I usually buy 8 1/2s out of caution, because of an old injury in my right foot. As I looked at these Moab 3's, I noticed Amazon recommended an 8, and I'll admit I pondered a few minutes whether to follow their recommendation before taking a leap of faith. I'm very happy I did, as these size 8's fit great, there's decent room in the toe box (which is critical for my injured foot), and no pinching anywhere.

They came brand new in a sealed box. I ordered the Smoke color, and on my laptop display, the mesh fabric in the Amazon picture looked like a cold gray, and the leather looked like warm brownish gray. The sole in the Amazon pic looked considerably darker than the uppers. In the shoes I received, the mesh fabric is more like a country blue (blue gray), and the leather is a warm gray color but not brownish as in the Amazon page. Also, the sole in the ones I received are closer to the color of the leather, but just a hair darker.

All in all they look and feel great. I'm very happy with this purchase, and the next time Amazon recommends a size, I'll be even more inclined to follow their recommendation.

title: Justify the price
body:
Having worn out a pair of Cole Haan split-toe oxfords over the course of four years, I decided to step up and order a pair of Allen Edmonds per the recommendation of fashion-savvy friends and colleagues. These have not disappointed over the past three months of use.

Although I was hesitant to shell out over $200 on a pair of dress shoes, you truly do get what you pay for with the FIfth Avenue Cap Toes. The shoe is constructed extremely well with high-grade materials. As with any fine shoe, they require breaking in but after about half a dozen wears, they start adapting to the size and movement of your foot and are quite comfortable as far as dress shoes go. The shoes also fit true to size.

Stylistically, I appreciate the pattern across the toe. It provides a subtle fashion contrast to the more staid simple line across the toe of standard cap toe shoes. Of course, that's a matter of personal taste.

Overall, I am extremely happy with the purchase. The value of the extra $100 you spend for a pair of Allen Edmonds over a similarly styled shoe will likely come to bear later on in the shoe's life as the construction is superior and the quality evident. Of course, if that does not turn out to be the case, I'll be sure to update the review!

title: Amazing craftmanship without being cloddy
body:
I am one of those people who will buy American whenever I can. It's often impossible.

Though I found my Allen Edwards Fifth Avenue Cap-Toe Oxford on Amazon, I was reluctant to buy them online. I wanted to get to the most comfortable fit as possible without returning and ordering shoes over and over. So I went to Lord and Taylor, and expensive department store that was the only place that carried the shoes locally.

I love these shoes! There was a breaking-in period which I think is one of the hallmarks of a well-made shoe, baseball glove, or anything made of leather. But is was long or particularly uncomfortable. I'm certainly not talking blisters.

True, I paid about a hundred dollars more doing it this way and $100 isn't chump change for me. But now I can order the proper size from Amazon without any hassles in finding the right fit.

As to price, $225 for a pair of shoes is still an extravagance for a lot of people, me included. To say that they will last longer than the cheap shoes from abroad, and so will even out, isn't fair to those struggling to pay bills. I can make a crappy pair of shoes last pretty long. But for once I wanted a well-made, American-made, pair of shoes that look and feel expensive, rather than always looking crappy.

Allen Edwards has an offer that when one has owned their shoes for a while, and they're beginning to look a little hang-dog, they'll rebuild them to the standards of new. That is a middling good deal at $150. At Amazon's prices, just buy a new pair.

title: The dress shoe to end all dress shoes: buy this shoe!
body:
Sizing:
Best bet is to go to a Nordstrom or whatever store nearby that carries AE's and get sized by one of the sales reps. If you haven't bought a pair of nice dress shoes before, your actual size is very likely not the size you've been wearing this whole time. The next best bet is to visit the AE website and print out their sizing chart (basically a paper version of a Brannock device). It's pretty accurate as long as you follow the instructions and don't screw up the aspect ratio when printing. What not to do: "Oh, I wear a 10.5 in Nike so I'm probably okay with a 10.5 in AE" -> this will lead to disappointment and gnashing of teeth.

Quality:
Barack Obama and George Bush (it's even party neutral!) were inaugurated wearing Allen Edmonds. The quality speaks for itself. Say goodbye to your rockports put together by a 10 year old in the Phillippines!

Color:
If you can, always try to see the colors in person. YMMV but the colors on websites are almost always not what you think they are. For example, Bourbon looks great online but (in my opinion) looks sub optimal in person.

Pricing:
Yeah, it's expensive, but this will be the last pair of dress shoes you buy in (literally) decades if you take care of them right. <-this is a lie, after owning a pair you will probably buy many more

Summary:
You should buy this shoe if:
-You want an amazingly crafted shoe guaranteed to garner compliments wherever you go
-You want a shoe dressy enough to wear to a wedding but versatile enough to wear to happy hour after work
-You're tired of blowing $150 on mall brand shoes that fall apart after a year of wear

You shouldn't buy this shoe if:
-It wouldn't let you make rent

BUY THIS SHOE!

title: nice if not defective, ALDEN is better
body: If money is no object and you want a really nice pair of shoes I have been buying Allen Edmond Soes as well as Alden shoes  for years. The Aldens are a bit pricier but the quality of the thick leather and the ability to retain form for many years makes them worth it. I have also bought Allen Edmonds which is a second best but did receive a defective pair that AE simply shipped back to me. When I tried them on they felt fine but once home (from San Francisco) I finally tried walking in them. They felt like they had a pebble under the ball of my foot. Feelng around I felt a metal object, sharp, pushing up through the footbed. I assume it is a nail. I sent them back to AE and they said they don't use nails except in the heel so sent them back. They were out of the one year warrenty but it was the first time I had worn them. They are returning them to me. Alden shoes carry a lifetime warrenty and if you simply wear them out, maybe the soles since the calfskin leather looks new after 20 years, they will rebuid them for you--presumably the sole. I would rate alden shoes 5 stars and AE shoes 4 star and there are plenty of other shoes with my 4 star rating that don't cost 1/2 as much.  ECCO comes to mind as an extremely comfortable (box toe construction) well made shoe about 1/2 the price. Both ECCO and Alden stand behind their shoes better than AE and you don't have to worry about a stray nail.

title: Flaws and imperfections present; Awaiting replacement pair
body:
Just received a pair of AE Fifth Avenue in Walnut and was quite disappointed. There were numerous imperfections, though the two largest and immediately noticeable problems were confined to the right shoe only. They didn't appear to be factory seconds, but I kind of got the impression that they were worn they had been worn around the house for a few hours and then returned.

The two largest issues were:

#1) A chip/crack in the wooden part of the sole (where the stitching is) on the right shoe. I noticed it almost immediately, as in no more than 7 seconds had passed since I opened the shoe box. If I was wearing them, the crack probably wouldn't look like a big deal to someone who was looking down at my shoes. However, it is a big deal and it was extremely visible upon visual inspection of the shoe (at eye level, of course).

#2) A vertical wrinkle or crease, also on the right shoe, that ran from the top line straight down the quarter to the start of the heel on the inside edge of the right shoe. This was a weird crease, because it wasn't a surface crease. It seemed to be structural in its origin, and was working itself outward toward the exterior.

These were more than enough to confirm that I needed to send them back and try my luck again. I'm waiting for the second pair to arrive, so I can compare them with the first (flawed) pair. I will then send the first pair back to Amazon, or I will send both pairs back to Amazon and get a refund.

I will update review when situation has resolved itself, for better or worse.

title: Club C85 are NOT the same as the C MemT
body: Usually in the Black/Black or White/Navy there's only a $5 to $6 difference between the Club C85 and the Club Memt . Though the shoes my look similar...they are NOT. There is a huge difference in the quality and wear. The C85 has a sewn/glued sole while the Memt has just a glued sole (look carefully at the top edge of the sole on both shoes). The C85 also has better ventilation. The C85 has good arch support for the average foot while the Memt has little to no arch support (If you have arch problems you may not like either style). I have been buying the Club C85 for +35 years...Because I was in a hurry (and their similar appearance) I made the mistake of getting the Club Memt at The Shoe Station in Florida and immediately returned them as soon as I put them on my feet. I almost made the same mistake here on Amazon. I've shown a couple of photos of my current C85's...Both pair were purchased in 2012 for $54 each at The Shoe Station in Tallahassee FL. The White/Navy are my go to daily shoes after work and all day at least one day out of every weekend. I wear the Black pair 4 to 6 times a month...Hope this helps in making your purchase.

title: What have they done to the aesthetics?
body:
I've been a big fan of the Ghost line for years and was looking forward to the 15 for a while. But the color options and overall aesthetics are truly awful. I'm sure they're a great shoe functionally but I'm going to have to pass on this generation of Ghosts. They're hideous.

[Edit] Well, I tried the a pair of the Brooks Glycerin 19's but I was very disappointed. I returned them and pulled the trigger on the Ghost 15's. I got a dark blue with yellow Brooks logo. Still not a fan of the overall appearance compared to previous Ghosts but I realized that this line just fits so well and is so comfortable for all day wear that there was really no other way to go. From a comfort standpoint they really have no equal and I guess, at the end of the day, that's what a quality sneaker is all about. I replaced the bright yellow laces with a pair of navy blue laces as the yellow ones were a bit over the top for my taste at least. Fit and finish is right up there with my previous Ghosts and the comfort just couldn't be better. So I'm going to change my rating to four stars as they continue to be the very best sneaker available from any brand at any price (I've tried Asics and Hoka and hated them both with a passion). Still had to deduct one star for this year's dismal aesthetics. I hope they rectify this with future generations of the Ghost.

title: Extremely comfy and light!
body:
Dear OnCloud,

I bought a pair of these running shoes from Zappos and they were almost $50 cheaper for the same shoe. They are extremely light and comfy. The unique thing about these shoes is that they come with regular laces not attached. The laces that come on the shoes are not tied and start only at the face of your foot and not down towards your toes like normal running shoes. I don’t know why they did it that way but it makes putting on these shoes super easy and quick. They are tight enough not to fall off my feet and I like the laces the way they come. On has traditional lace running shoes but those require you tie them each time you wear them. I love that you can just slip these on with minimal effort. They are super lightweight, supportive, and comfy. My wife also has a pair and we have had our fair share of tennis shoes but these are by far the best. They weren’t made in America but that’s ok for me. They look real nice and they are wide enough for my feet. I wear a size 10US an they fit as expected. The arch is also very nice and the insole is nicely padded. I had Underarmor running shoes that connected to my iPhone 13Pro which would monitor how much I would run but these don’t have it which is ok. I don’t go running that much and I just needed a pair of running shoes that’s comfy, supportive, and durable enough to last me a few years. At the price, I would get my moneys worth if I can use these for 2yrs. I work from home full-time and I don’t really leave the house so they won’t see much use other than when I go running with the wife. Overall, these shoes look nice, they’re supportive, have nice insoles, bounce, and they are super light. Can’t speak to the durability but I have no doubt they will last me a couple years with my usage.

Thanks for allowing me to leave a feedback on these running shoes.

title: Fantastic Running Companion: Under Armour Running Shoes
body:
I recently purchased a pair of Under Armour running shoes and I am extremely impressed with their performance. These shoes have proven to be a game-changer in my running routine, offering exceptional comfort, support, and durability.

First and foremost, the level of comfort these shoes provide is unmatched. The cushioning system incorporated in the midsole ensures a plush and responsive feel that absorbs impact effectively. It aids in minimizing fatigue, allowing me to push harder and longer during my runs. The padded collar and tongue also contribute to a snug fit and enhanced ankle support, preventing any discomfort or rubbing.

Stability and support are paramount for any running shoe, and this is where Under Armour shines. The combination of a solid outsole with excellent traction and a well-constructed upper provides exceptional stability. These shoes offer a secure fit, preventing any slips or movements that could lead to injury. My foot feels locked in place, enabling me to confidently tackle different terrains and maintain a consistent pace.

Durability is another aspect that stood out to me. Despite intense use on various surfaces, the shoe's construction has remained intact and shows no signs of wear. The high-quality materials used in the upper, midsole, and outsole are undoubtedly built to last. This long-lasting reliability ensures that the shoes will serve me well for many miles to come.

Moreover, the sleek design of the Under Armour running shoes is worth mentioning. Its aesthetic appeal is a bonus, as these shoes look stylish and modern while offering high functionality. The brand's attention to detail is evident in the thoughtful design, making these shoes suitable for both running and everyday wear.

In conclusion, Under Armour running shoes have exceeded my expectations in terms of comfort, support, and durability. They provide a comfortable running experience, superb stability, and impressive longevity. Whether you're a seasoned runner or just starting out, I highly recommend giving Under Armour running shoes a try. They will undoubtedly enhance your running performance and keep you going mile after mile.

title: These are a decent pair of sneakers but they definitely need some improvements.
body:
All right today. What I have for everyone is my full review of the Saucony Men's Ride 16 Sneakers. Now what I've decided to do for this review is break it down into the positives and the negatives associated with the sneakers. Then I'm going to talk about the overall pricing and current availability. Then I'm going to share my overall final thoughts and make an overall recommendation. That being said, I hope everyone finds this review helpful and without further ado, let's begin.

Positives:
The overall design of the sneakers is really good. They offer a really good amount of support while also being made out of breathable material. Other than that I do have to say I do like the overall look of the sneakers the white and black color scheme with the subtle touches of orange I do think overall the sneakers look really good. Okay I think that about sums up all the deposits now let's move on and talk about some of the negatives of these sneakers.

Negatives:
Now in my time with these sneakers there are two major negatives that I came across. The first one being although the sneakers do offer a lot of support and are made out of breathable material. Overall I would have to say in my experience they are not very comfortable wearing them for extended periods of time they do tend to squeeze the upper part of my feet no matter how loose I laced them up or how much slack I get out of the tongue. They still squeeze the upper part of my feet and over time become very uncomfortable. So I would have to say that that was probably one of the biggest major negatives that I've experienced I was expecting the sneakers to be overall a lot more comfortable based on what they're supposed to be used for exercising and running which is what I do a lot of primarily. So I was really disappointed. The other negative of the sneakers in my opinion is the price now these sneakers are roughly selling for $139.99 or just to make it easier roughly a little bit over $140. Now I can understand that when your sneakers is made out of a certain type of material that can have a tendency to raise the price especially if you make it out of materials that are supposed to be a lot more durable and breathable and stretchy but you still want them to hold up in the long run. But at least for me I feel like that price is a little steep and then you mix that with the fact that overall they were extremely uncomfortable for me those were two major negatives again that had me overall this feeling disappointed. All right I think that summarizes all of the negatives. Now let's get into the final part of this review let's go.
All right overall how do I feel about the
Saucony Men's Ride 16 Sneakers? Well as I said earlier the sneakers do offer a really good design with an overall really good amount of support and they look really good as well, but for me the major thing when we talk about sneakers is the overall comfort and be to the fact that overall I found these sneakers to be very uncomfortable I would have to say when I talk about how I feel about them based on just the comfort level alone I would have to say I don't like them and then you add to that the fact that they are kind of steeply priced. title: Nice shoes. More stable than Hoka
body:
Review update: The weather was cooperating this evening so I took these out for a 5.5 mile run. I'm very impressed to be honest. They are definitely more stable than the Hoka's I have and, even though they don't feel like they have as much shock support, they performed very well. No unusual aches or pains. They do feel a bit different in my ankles, but that's likely due to the difference in the heel support/feel that I mentioned in my first review. Surprisingly my average pace was about 15 seconds per mile faster than my most recent runs in the Hoka's. That said, I can't say that little bit of difference was due to the shoes. It could just be me feeling more energetic. But they definitely didn't perform worse than the Hoka's.

Original review: I'm an avid jogger and walker - typically running at least 6 miles or walking 7 miles every other day (the other days I'm on my bike). My regular go to shoe is Hoka so that's what I'm comparing these to.
I wear an 11.5 and these fit properly, although where a little narrow feeling when I put them on the first time. They did loosen up nicely after my first 7 mile walk in them. Now they fit very comfortably.
The first thing I noticed is they definitely feel very different than my Hoka's (I have a few different model Hoka). The sole is where I feel the biggest difference. Almost like these have different support points in the sole than Hoka. Not uncomfortable, just different. I do wish they had a little more arch support though.
The biggest difference is these feel much more stable than my Hoka's. The downside is they also don't seem to have as much cushioning/shock support. That is probably why they feel more stable though. I haven't jogged in them yet, but I suspect I'll probably feel some impact pain near the end of the run due to them not having as much cushioning in the sole. But maybe I'll be surprised? The 7 mile walk was very comfortable and was at the same pace (4 miles per hour) as with Hoka. No pain or unusual fatigue. They actually made me feel more confident in the walk due to the greater feeling of support.
They definitely aren't as flashy as the Hoka's I have, so that's either a plus or minus depending on your tastes. Me, I prefer bright and flashy mostly for visibility reasons. I want car drivers to be able to see me as easily as possible.

title: Great shoe, relatively low arch, inside posting
body:
I ordered these for my husband who runs a great deal (80+ marathon completions). The feedback below is from him.

The shoe fits nicely and as expected. I do wear running shoes a couple of sizes larger than everyday shoes to protect my toenails. They do include a top wrap which hugs your foot nicely as advertised. Running shoe fit is very personal for everyone, but these match my need perfectly. They include a bit of extra posting on the interior which helps with my overpronation. They do not include a really high arch and I find this very comfortable. The shape of the lower back of the heal is perfect for foot strike runners to roll through each stride. The cushioning is excellent without being too soft for comfortable running.

The uppers breathe nicely to keep your feet cool. The laces with the top wrap hold them securely on your feet without binding or slipping.

This is a first class running shoe. After having run for years in a different shoe, there is a good chance I will switch to this entirely.

title: Really ASICS? Unattractive & poorly designed toe boxes
body:
They look great as long as you don't stand up or use the shoe as a shoe...

(First pic is of the 1st order that I returned/replaced.) This is what they looked like straight out of the box. ~Collapsing toe box on left shoe.

(2nd pics are of the 2nd pair I received & will be returning.) They were worn inside for 2 days.. So around 16 hours of gentle use. ~Collapsing toe boxes on both shoes.

The shoes are the correct size and are actually rather comfortable. Although, once you stand up and/or start walking around the quality of the toe box design becomes quite apparent and looks rather cheap and poorly made.

The 2nd pair I received has a nice hard lump sewn inside the heel of the left shoe as well which tears up your heel by stabbing into it.

I have never experienced or even seen these issues with any of the other well known competitors/brands.

Unsure what to do at this point... Am I really just being sent lemons or is there a design flaw with these shoes???

*Update: If you contact ASICS to ask if there is a design flaw with these shoes... They will suggest that you are just wearing them incorrectly. Wearing the shoes incorrectly?? I've only been wearing shoes for 40+ years... LOL

Save your time and money by not purchasing these shoes!

title: It is leather and it will relax!
body:
Usually I'm a 9.5 and sometimes a 10. When I received this pair and tried, it was on the small side and my first impulse was to ship them back. It was cold outside so I did not try them. After a while I decided to wear them for a bit in the home. Then I used them a couple of times just to walk my dog in the neighborhood. Finally I decided to use a thin sock and take them to work from morning till noon a couple of times and initial pain and discomfort started slowly to go away. It is leather and it will relax! Today, for the first time, I decided to wear them for a whole day, and so far, after 6 hours, my feet are felling good. I think now they are a perfect snug fit, still not painful or with discomfort, and believe me when I say that my feet are very picky regarding the comfort and breathability of my shoes. The sole is thin and soft, so if you intend to walk on hard irregular surface, I would suggest something else.
If I would buy again perhaps I would get a size 10 just to avoid the initial pain of making them wearable, but not sure if for that size the leather will relax/enlarge how I would feel? Like in a BOAT?

title: Great fit, excellent quality, butter soft
body:
This shoe fits me like a glove. The first day I wore them, yesterday, I did not want to take them off...and didn't. Material and construction are excellent. The leather is butter soft. There was no break in period, just lace up and walk. And god, they are beautiful.
I have 5 other pairs of AE shoes and have found that fit is highly dependent upon the last. Just because this pair of size 13 B 5th Ave. captoes fit like a glove is no predictor that AEs constructed on different lasts will fit as well.
Similarly, quality of materials and construction varies with the style. Overall, AEs are very high quality, but I have pair of monkstraps made with very thick leather and soles that refuse to flex.
And I continue to buy AEs because south of $500 a pair, there are no better shoes made in the US.

title: Best Crocs for A Short Girly
body:
**Pros:**
- **Comfortable:** These Crocs are incredibly comfortable to wear. The cushioned sole provides excellent support for your feet, making them perfect for long walks or standing for extended periods.
- **Easy to Clean:** The material is easy to wipe clean, which is great for outdoor activities or messy situations. You don't have to worry about dirt or mud ruining your shoes.
- **Adjustable Straps:** The straps on these Crocs are a game-changer. They allow you to customize the fit to your liking, ensuring that your feet stay secure and comfortable.
- **Tall Design:** The tall design of these Crocs offers additional protection for your feet, making them suitable for activities where you might encounter rough terrain or debris.

**Cons:**
- **Style:** While functionality is great, the tall design of these Crocs might not be everyone's cup of tea in terms of style. They can look a bit chunky and may not be suitable for more formal occasions.
- **Breathability:** The tall design, while protective, might hinder breathability a bit. Your feet might get warmer in these compared to traditional open-style Crocs.
- **Bulkiness:** The additional height and straps could make these Crocs feel a bit bulkier and heavier than the standard models, which might not be preferable for those looking for lightweight footwear.

Price/value-wise: I’m not sure it’s totally worth the extra $15+ over the classic, especially since you can only get white or black right now, but I got it $20 off for sale so it was a no-brainer!

title: Hiking Crocs
body: I purchased this particular style because it looked as though it had extra or thicker soles and/or heel support. I don't hike however I stand up or walk 10 1/2 hrs or more a day while I'm working. I started wearing Crocs when I got awful heel pain and found a style (that has since been discontinued) that totally alleviated my pain. I have tried a few other work Crocs that didn't help so when I saw these I thought I'd try them. I didn't have foot pain however it wasn't long before something else started to happen. While wearing the shoes after about 4 or 5 days they started to throw my balance out of whack. Meaning while standing in them my weight would shift slightly inward on both sides. Because of the slant my knees would knock a little throwing my hips, knees and back out of whack. Thus making me walk like a penguin. It was so painful I couldn't wear them. It was nice not having any foot pain, however the other pain was unbearable. Perhaps it was just a faulty pair and I might try ordering another at some point. Just afraid of wasting another $60.

title: Awesome sandals!
body:
Bought these for our 4 year old nephew in size 2-3.

If you are new to Rainbow sandals, you should know that if you purchase the size that fits you, the strap will be very tight and uncomfortable. However, if you are able to bear the discomfort for a few days, these sandals will be one of the most comfortable and durable sandals you will wear once broken in. Also, personally, I've owned several pairs of these sandals (in adult sizes) and they last for a couple years AT LEAST with almost daily usage, and the strap has held strong on all of them.

Having said this, we did not want to subject our nephew to this kind of "break-in discomfort" especially since he is new to sandals and that his feet are growing quite rapidly, but we wanted to get him his own Rainbows because he wanted to be just like us =). So, the size we got him is a bit bigger than his feet, but he is able to wear them comfortably now and they will break in slowly as his feet get larger.

title: V5 is better than the V3
body:
I purchased the New Balance 680 V3 more than 1.5 years ago. I recently purchased the V5 to replace the V3.

The V5 is an improvement over V3. Why? The V5 has a softer, more cushy removable insert than the V3. (The footbed/insert of the V3 felt like walking on concrete). The insert/footbed of the V3 was so hard I replaced it with a softer insert I purchased online. However, the insert of the V5 is much softer and I did not need to replace.

One thing I like about the New Balance 680 is that it has a wide toe box. (Which is kind of boxy or squarish). In contrast; while the Asics GT-2000 4 and 5 I have, tapper or narrow much more in the toe box. As such, the New Balance 680 is more comfortable in hot weather when your feet swell/expand, since the toe box is wider.

While the Asics GT-2000 is a really nice shoe and very comfortable; the New Balance 680 is more comfortable when the weather is hot.

title: very comfortable, runs narrow
body:
A very comfortable lightweight runner, but it's narrow at my normal medium-width size 10.5.

The shoe hugs the foot and feels reasonably supportive. The aesthetic of the gray color is understated (almost to the point of drab since the material is matte). That's a positive or negative depending on your taste. The length is true to size.

The width is the only issue, and I wish there was just a little extra material. Compared to my other runners, the top of the shoe (past the arch towards the toes) starts immediately crossing the foot, rather than rising straight up before crossing the foot. That makes for a slightly squashed feel across the toes. I'm used to ASICS, where the 10.5-Medium fits as expected. I'm not sure if the narrowness is a New Balance thing, or if it's meant to stretch to fit? Maybe the manufacturer can chime in...

Depending on how this new shoe breaks in with wear (or doesn't), I may upgrade or downgrade my rating.

title: Excellent Workout Shoe
body: This is exactly what I was looking for in a workout shoe. I have owned the 680v3 for more than a year and do notice some differences. The previous version 3 is more of a running shoe than this model (version 5) due to a more areo-dynamic design and more narrow overall footprint in the version 3. This version has a larger overall footprint due to a slightly wider width at the front vols of the foot. This is noticeably helpful when you need to balance on one foot (like when doing single leg squats, or lunges, especially with dumbbells/weights) The reinforcements around the exterior toe are more sturdy, which makes the whole front foot wobble less during forward movements than did the version 3. The abzorb cushioning in the rear vols of the foot feel more absorbent than the version 3, which is noticeably handy when doing  plyo/jumping exercises. This version is a tad beefier looking and does feel slightly heavier than the version 3, but it is still a sleek and very light shoe. A heavier person could use these as a running shoe and it would be just fine. A more swifter runner may find the previous version more suitable. I use my version 3s for running. But the version 5 is my choice as a workout shoe--they are great! Just be sure to get your correct size :-)

I have wide feet, but my toes bumped up against inside of the size 9 shoes. I'm debating if I should just return them again and get like size 10.5? That just seems ridiculous.

Another weird thing: no loop in the back to pull them on with. You have to buy a shoe horn I guess, or just smash them with your heels. It's a bizarre oversight since obviously hikers don't carry shoe horns around...

They are exactly what they look like: basically jungle mocs with the sole from the hiking boots.

title: BEFORE YOU ORDER THESE SHOES BEWARE
body:
Before you order anything from this company make sure you understand their return policy!!!
I ordered a pair that was my normal size shoe, these were about a size too big. I wore them 3 times to make sure I was right about the size.
Decided to return them for a size one size smaller. I just wanted an exchange, I liked the shoes. The list of requirements to receive a full refund was absolutely unbelievable.
The box has to be inmint condition. The shipping paperwork has to be included. There can be no signs that they have been worn. The list has about 10 requirements and every one must be met.
I wrote them and told them I will keep the shoes because I could not meet all of their requirements, but that I would never again buy anything they make.
I hope you don't throw away $100.00 like I did.

title: 574s Not The Same, Way Too Small
body:
Got these for my son as he has had 4 pairs of New Balance 574s over many years. He usually wears a 10.5M, but felt he now needed some more toe room, so according to New Balance's website, going up a half size and getting a wide would provide a little over .25 of an inch of extra space in width in the toe box, plus a little under that of more space in length, providing more room in the toe box. The problem is, these shoes were in-fact smaller than his 10.5M 574s, which makes no sense, so we returned them; they also came with pink ink on the laces and a dent in the toe box that was rock solid. The side of the heel, where it angles up was also rock solid in some areas where it's usually soft and pliable. New Balance definitely changed the last on all new versions of the 574.

See pictures for how New Balance is completely shrinking all of their shoes. This was the second pair we had to return for sizing that seemed like a massive defect. My son has stuck with New Balance for years because of the room and support provided in their sneakers, but now will be looking to other brands because of this fiasco.

I would not recommend these sneakers to anyone because they are not the same as the usual 574s we all know.

title: SIZES EXPLAINED
body:
These shoes did not fit me and here's why...

SIZES EXPLAINED:

New Balance put most of their popular retro cool shoes into the hands of Asian manufacturers, so the sizing on these models is completely off:

574, 363, 501, 565, 515

That is why you will find so many reviews stating the fit is "too tight" and "too small" and several people explaining how they were too tight and too small even though they ordered a size larger and wider than usual like 2E or even 4E extra width sizes.

I found a website explaining this but since links may get removed in a product review, I'm just explaining what I learned.

The only people who are not going to think the sizing is off are people who have been buying these lines for the last 10 or 15 years and already are used to the weird sizing. These sizes are completely different from the New Balance models made in the USA or UK.

576, 577 and 996 are all Made in the USA or UK and will be very comfortable and regularly sized. They will also be much more expensive. New Balance models made in the USA or UK will almost always be over $100, typically about $139 and sometimes on sale for as low as $79, but never lower than that unless it's the most unpopular design ever... For example, there is one model of 996 on Amazon right now that looks nothing like a retro cool sneaker; I have no idea why they called it a '996' anything. It looks like a futuristic mini-van:[[ASIN:B00LNRN3PS New Balance Men's MC996 Lightweight Tennis Shoe, Grey/Green, 10 2E US]]. So, if you're looking at a shoe with price range of $39 - $79, chances are that it is Asian made and the size will be too small and too tight.

I have skinny feet and if I am ordering any cheap shoes from New Balance, I have to order 1 full size larger and at least 2E width, which is still a bit tight. 4E width would be better, but they rarely have those for sale on Amazon in my size. To put that in perspective, my dress shoe size is 9.5 or 10. Since these retro-cool New Balances are supposed to be running shoes, it makes sense that you would follow the typical advice to buy one size larger, so size 11 makes sense...right? The problem is this isn't exactly right. Size 10 fits me extremely well length-wise for walking, but are way too tight. Why would I want running shoes in walking size? Because most people actually wear these retro cool shoes as casual sneakers. However, you basically have to buy one full size up and extra wide to fit even skinny feet, so that makes your casual kicks slightly longer at the toe box than feels necessary, but it's not too bad. It's nowhere near the same comfy fit as you would find on a pair of USA-made 576 New Balances, though.

Having shoes that are too tight in the metatarsal area is very bad for your feet and lead to problems like plantar fasciitis. So, for the Asian-made New Balances such as 574, 363, 501, 565, 515, etc., it is much better for your feet to have "room to grow" in front of your toes (as if you're a little kid buying shoes) rather than having the arch area placed in the wrong spot and squeezing the heck out of the front part of your foot at the metatarsal area.

TOO LONG, DIDN'T READ VERSION:

These Asian-made models will be too small and too tight: 574, 363, 501, 565, 515
These USA/UK-made models will be correctly sized (and cost twice as much): 576, 577 and 996

Before wasting your time trying to "break in" your new kicks, head on over to New Balances' own website (do a web search for 'New Balance Size Guide' and scroll down to the bottom and read the first bullet point):

• New Balance shoes are made to fit directly out of the box. They do not need to be broken in.

If they are too tight, they are Asian-made, so just return them while you still can and get 1 size larger and 2E or 4E width instead of D width.

title: A++! SUPER COMFY
body:
Disclosure: I am a female that buys these MENS NB.

What can I say, I love these shoes and have been buying them for 10+ years. I have probably 5 pairs of them. They're incredibly comfortable for all day wear. And of top notch quality. The only reason I keep buying them isn't because the shoe fails in ANY way over years of use. Literally, nothing has failed. No separation of sole, no separation of anything with daily use with every pair I've owned. In all reality, I'm really not nice to my shoes. So, needless to say I typically buy many pairs because of something I do that's dumb. The last pair had an unfortunate event with paint.

Disclosure 2: I do not use these for running. Again, a woman wearing a mens shoe likely isn't going to provide the right running fit. The perfect day-to-day use fit, yes. But not running. I find they tend to be too lose to run and I end up getting shin splints. I can, however, use them for a wide variety of other workouts as they do provide standing and limited movement stability. Not running though. Other reviews by men may be able to provide you more insight into its effectiveness.

However, I will say the as a woman and I always buy the men's NB. They're just far cooler than the women's. MUCH better colors. (by the way, take note New Balance, not all women want 8 different neon colors on one shoe. Nor do they want to look like a teenager threw up on their shoes). Even with wearing mens' shoes, they fit REALLY well. Super happy, A+ for men's. F+ for women's. Or if you're a glass half full kinda person, D- for women's.

Ladies size 9.5, Mens NB size 8M D

title: Most Painful Boot Ever.
body: I decided to buy these boots to wear to work (metal fab). I have been a Keen guy for over a decade now and while Keens are great waterproof and built like a tank boots, they have basically zero breathability, and I was sick of smelling hot dumpster smell everyday when i got home and took my boots off. having been a Footwear Department Manager at Gander Mountain back when that was still a thing, i knew that Merril Moab Vents supposedly had legendary beathability, and seeing as i had sold literally Hundreds of them to customers, and the fact that they were on sale for cheap, I thought this was going to be a home run. I was badly mistaken. The second day wearing these I had a bit a foot pain, nothing unusual when you are breaking in a hiking boot. But then every day the pain increased. After two weeks of wearing these, the pain became excruciating. I had to stop wearing them, and the pain continued in my feet for an additional 3 days after I stopped wearing these. I have NEVER experienced pain like this from footwear in all my years. For this reason I cannot recommend these boots. I hope that my case is an anomaly and everyone else is enjoying their boots with no problem. Perhaps i was just the one unlucky one who received a bad pair of shoes that snuck their way through inquality control. I will be purchasing a pair of Keens to replace these. Never again Merril.

title: I recommend the shoe, but not for my feet
body:
Shoe reviews have 2 sides - objective and subjective, the subjective is of course how they fit your feet, and mileage may vary.
So the Moab 3, it is very well made, good materials, looks good.
The soles are grippy, don't squeak on floors, and convey a sense of stability when walking.
The length of the shoe is spot on to size.

Now the more subjective part:
The width is very good for me, I walk barefoot and with Merrell's barefoot shoes. My feet are more bony than meaty, so the volume of the shoe is a bit large for me. This has been the direction merrell has taken in the last 10 years or so. Tightening the laces works to a point but then the shoe fabric can start to pucker. Thicker socks.

The toes have good room to move, but even so, the taper to the shoe's toe is a bit aggressive on the big toe, it starts to go in too soon. My toe has a touch of arthritis so I'm sensitive to this. The Moab 3 is just on the good side of the equation here.

And then the biggest flaw, for me: there is a seam where heel meets the rest of the shoe, which carries into a hump/bump/thick part in the sole. This sticks up into the instep, and probably is usually a good thing as it forms a part of the arch support. For me this is too far back, and starts to hurt my heels.

Was this the insoles? I tried different ones and I still have the same result. I will need to modify some to counteract this hump.

Merrell has felt like this on my feet for the last decade, in their constructed shoes. The arch support is too aggressively lumpy at the heel end, for my feet. I was hesitant in ordering the Moab 3 for this reason, but decided to buy anyway. Unfortunately if I'm to buy more Merrell shoes in the future I will have to do it in person, so I can test for this problem.

I recommend these shoes highly, for most people they should be an excellent choice.

title: NOT Waterproof, wet socks.
body:
These are so disappointing.....wet right foot on day 1.
Straight out the box, day 1, walking on wet grass and through the occasional sole height puddle (1/2 inch to 1 inch deep), these shoes leaked and my socks were wet, but only on the right foot. Toes stayed dry, but mid foot, underside of sock was wet.
Shoes themselves are incredibly comfortable and look great, but I bought them specifically for walking the dogs on the trails when wet or damp from morning dew.
Fortunately Amazon offered try before you buy, so I brushed them off repacked them and sent them back within two days.
Tried them on the second day just to make sure that I didn't get water over the side, I was able to confirm they did leaked just along the sole and upper seam at mid foot on the right shoe.
At least the Moab 2s that I was replacing kept their waterproof properties for 3 month before giving up.
Summary, Merrell did not improve the waterproof feature on these shoes over the Moab 2.
Waterproof 0 out of 5
Comfort 5 out of 5
If you want comfortable trail shoes without waterproofing, these would be a winner, avoid if using in the wet.

FYI
Quality Shoes run true to foot measurement, which tends to be smaller than the less expensive brands. Shoes made inexpensively routinely run a half size larger, if you measure a 6, the 6.5 fits.
Sam Edelman makes a HIGH QUALITY Shoe. Sax 5th Ave carries his shoes. 🏆

A Shoe Tip: ✔ When purchasing a "Loafer style shoes" (that's Leather) Soak a Wash Cloth in very Hot Water, wring out bout leave enough water to dampen the inside area of the shoe, avoiding the sole area. Place foot right in and wear for at least an hour or so.
(The shoe molds to design of your foot), it prevents any "New-Shoe Blisters" and gains a comfort level of a shoe that's been "broken-in".
A true Shoe Salesperson in a Department Store taught me this back in the 1980's and as a result, I have never suffered blisters since.

Just a share of info I hope can be helpful.

Happy Hunting! 😘
PS. ... Edelman is my maiden name, I was so thrilled when I saw the 1st pair at a Sax in Florida. Nothing like having "Surname Signature Shoes"! Go Sam! 😁

title: YMMV but comfy & classy
body:
I got these shoes for my first "big time adult" work shoes to have as flats for days when I knew I would be walking a lot and therefore uninterested in heels. they totally do the trick! when I first got them, I thought they might be slightly too small but they have a little bit of stretch and now fit me absolutely perfectly which makes them very comfortable!

I have a friend who also has them and she says hers rub the back of her ankle a little and are slightly loose - she put a bandaid on the inside back of the shoe and is having no issues now.

I wore these for 4 days of training where I was walking and standing A LOT and my feet never hurt at all. also, I spotted them on a bunch of other girls so it seems like theres a general consensus that people like them. if you have high arches, these may not be the most supportive shoe but I think an insole could totally fix that problem. I don't have a high arch so not sure

they've very classy and understated as well. considering the price tag of so many comparable shoes and the quality of these, I think its a great bang for your buck.

title: Most comfortable shoes for any occasion - Just buy them already!
body:
So...like an idiot, I forgot to pack my sneakers on a recent trip to Lisbon. And, Lisbon is not a place you want to be without comfortable shoes if you plan on exploring the city - LOTS of hills. Lucky for me, I packed these loafers aka my absolute favorite shoes in terms of comfortable, versatility, style, etc., etc.

I wore them for a majority of the trip, including the many hours my husband and I spent pushing our two year old up and down hill after hill in her stroller. Was I tired? Yes, very much so. Did my feet hurt? Not one bit - and that's saying a lot for someone who is exceptionally prone to blisters.

These fit true to size. I wear a size nine in most shoes and the nine fit like a glove. They were comfortable from the first time I wore them, which is crucial since I don't have the time or patience to break in shoes. They are also super cute and affordable. I have a pair in all the basic/neutral colors available and they've held up great even with me wearing them just about daily to work, business trips (super easy to pack!), vacations, errands, etc.

I can't recommend them enough especially for working mamas constantly on the go. Buy them - you will not regret it!

title: 5 stars!
body:
I recently purchased the New Balance Women's 574 Core Sneaker, and I am extremely impressed with their quality, comfort, and style. These sneakers are perfect for any occasion, whether you're running errands, working out, or just need a comfortable pair of shoes for everyday wear.

The 574 Core Sneaker is made of high-quality materials that are both durable and breathable, ensuring that my feet stay cool and comfortable throughout the day. The design is stylish and versatile, making it easy to pair with any outfit.

What I love most about these sneakers is the level of support and cushioning they provide. The ENCAP midsole technology offers excellent support for my feet and helps absorb shock, making them perfect for running and other high-impact activities.

The fit is also true to size, and the shoes are easy to slip on and off. I appreciate that they come in a variety of colors, so I can choose a pair that matches my personal style.

Overall, I highly recommend the New Balance Women's 574 Core Sneaker to anyone looking for a comfortable, stylish, and durable pair of sneakers. The quality and support are unmatched, and they are the perfect addition to any wardrobe. Five stars!

The right shoe was no problem. It has gotten so bad, I can no longer wear these shoes. I find myself having to pay for another pair, in half a size larger, hoping they will fit. I will return them immediately if they don't, rather than waiting a week or two. I don't know if this was an aberration in the making of the shoe, or what, but the left shoe was DEFINITELY too small.
Just a post script here. I contacted the seller (Zappos) after seeing their return policy and was delighted to see that they will accept the return of my shoes that didn't fit, and give me a refund. Thank you Zappos!!!

title: What I expected for now
body:
I bought these to replace several pairs of reef and olukai flops I've had over the years. I've noticed that most those flops had a felt type glue down foot bed that started to peel off and get annoying after 1 summer of use everytime.

So far these meet my expectations, they do not have that foot bed liner glued on and appear to be a solid piece of material for the entire foot bed and a separate material for the sole. I took a chance and bought a size smaller than normal and they go on snug but feel fine when moving and under weight.

I am hoping these will be similar to the old reef playa negra that lasted me nearly 4 years and we're a standard sole and foot bed without that annoying glue down thing that peels within weeks of being wet.

title: Well Respected Product Name

The sandals are as described and along with other reviewers I do find them quite comfortable to wear.  Unlike my former pair, they do not seem to be slippery when wet (but I haven't taken them to the pool yet.)  One slightly odd note is that these are marked "size 11" and in length and width of the sole, they are the same as my two previous pair of size 11's -- so, good.  However, the over the top strap on these size 11's is noticeably quite a bit more snug on my foot than the strap on the two previous pair (not from Reef).  I can get my foot in, and that's enough.  But the strap does feel snug on the foot.

title: A little expensive, but worth it. My new favorite footwear.
body:
I've owned these for a month and they've been to the pool, beach and supermarket. They took about a week to break in (they squeaked a bit). And now, the squeaking has stopped and I can confidently say they are maybe the best pair I've ever owned. And living in Florida, I've owned many pairs of sandals.

They look great (I needed a brown pair), have great arch support, are very comfortable and seem durable (they've survived chlorine, salt water, sand and Miller Lite so far). I bought them one size larger than my usual shoe size to protect my toes from getting stubbed. I'm a little clumsy.

They're priced a little higher than I usually spend on sandals. But so far, are worth it.

title: Rubbed my toe raw

What's also interesting is that my room mate for the trip bought new Reef slip-ons and had the same issue on the side of their foot.  Material quality issues?  I would have expected this result from cheap sandals which is why I bought Reef.  The arch support was there, but doesn't do any good if you can't wear them.

title: Very comfortable!
body: I ordered these before a trip to Punta Cana - risky considering new flip flops have the potential to not fit well.  I typically wear an 8.5, but ordered an 8.  They seemed a little on the small size, but honestly fit fine!  I wore them through the airport, the many lines for security/customs/etc., and all week long on vacation.  They're the most comfortable flip flops I've ever owned - lots of arch support and no rubbing or chafing.  They were also super grippy around a wet pool - both on the ground, and the surface where my foot touches the top of the flip flop.  I'm already looking forward to ordering another pair!  A little on the pricey side, but well worth the money!
